It seems venerable [Note: [Col. 0517] The word *enim* (“indeed”) is absent in 3 and G.] that regular communities and canonical communities should have places in different regions for receiving guests, pilgrims, and the poor [Note: [Col. 0517] 1*, Rem., Pith., and Paris. have *susceptiones hospitum, peregrinorum et pauperum* (“places for receiving guests, pilgrims, and the poor”).], because the Lord himself will say at the reward of the great day: “I was a guest, and you received me” [Note: [Col. 0517] 3 has *dicit: hospes* (“he says: I was a guest”), with the remainder absent; 1* has *rememoratione* (“remembrance”) instead of *remuneratione* (“reward”).].

And the apostle, praising hospitality, said: “Through this some pleased God” [Note: [Col. 0517] 6 adds “and his angels”], when they received angels as guests [Note: [Col. 0517] 3 has *apostolus per hanc, inquit, placuerunt Deo* (“the apostle says, through this they pleased God”).].

### 71. On Abbesses Acting Contrary to the Custom of the Church of God

It has been heard that certain abbesses, contrary to the custom of the holy Church of God [Note: [Col. 0517] B has *amorem* (“love”) instead of *morem* (“custom”).] [Note: [Col. 0517] *sanctae* (“holy”) is absent in 3.], give blessings, impose hands, and make the sign of the holy cross over men’s heads, and also veil virgins with a priestly blessing. Know that this must absolutely be forbidden by you, most holy fathers, in your dioceses.

### 72. On Clerics Who Pretend to Be Monks

Clerics who pretend by habit or name to be monks, but are not, must in every respect, it seems, be corrected and reformed [Note: [Col. 0517] 4, G, Reg., Bell., Colb., Trec., Sang., and Camb. have *corrigantur atque emendentur* (“must be corrected and reformed”).], so that they may be either true monks or true canons [Note: [Col. 0517] 1, 1*, and B have this word order; 3 has other arrangements of the words.].

### 73. On False Writings and Doubtful Narratives

False writings and doubtful narratives, or those wholly contrary to the Catholic faith—for example, that most wicked and utterly false letter which, after the past year, certain deluded persons, leading others into error, were saying had fallen from heaven—must neither be believed nor read [Note: [Col. 0517] 1 has *et nec* (“and neither”) instead of *nec* (“nor”).], but must be burned [Note: [Col. 0517] 4 has *comburentur* (“they are burned”) instead of *comburantur* (“let them be burned”).], lest the people be led into error by such a writing.

Only canonical books, Catholic treatises, and the authority and sayings of the saints [Note: [Col. 0517] B has *auctoritates* (“authorities”); 1* has *edicta sanctorum* (“decrees of the saints”).] are to be read and transmitted [Note: [Col. 0517] G inserted here the words “but only the canonical books, Catholic treatises, and the authority and sayings of the saints,” omitted in this place, in chapter 75 after “be fulfilled.”].

### 74. On the Roman Chant to Be Performed by Monks

The monks are to perform the Roman chant fully and in orderly fashion in the nocturnal or gradual office, in accordance with what our father of blessed memory, King Pippin [Note: [Col. 0517] “Our father of blessed memory” is omitted in Bal.], strove to have done [Note: [Col. 0517] 3 and Met. have *decrevit* (“decreed”).], when he removed the Gallican chant [Note: [Col. 0519] The words are absent in 1*.], for the sake of unanimity with the Apostolic See and the peaceful concord of the holy Church of God.

### 75. On Servile Works That Must Not Be Done on Sundays

We also decree, according to what the Lord commanded in the Law, that servile works must not be done on Sundays, just as my father of blessed memory commanded in his synodal edicts [Note: [Col. 0519] 4 and G have *ut* (“that”) instead of *quod* (“that”).]: neither shall men perform rural labor [Note: [Col. 0519] 6, G, and Bal. add *opera* (“work”).], nor cultivate a vineyard [Note: [Col. 0519] 4 and G have *in colendo* (“in cultivating”); 6 has *nec vineam colendam* (“nor a vineyard to be cultivated”); Bal. has *nec vineam colendo* (“nor in cultivating a vineyard”).], nor plow in the fields, nor reap [Note: [Col. 0519] 1 has *metente* (“while reaping”).], nor cut hay, nor build a hedge [Note: [Col. 0519] B has *sepe componendo* (“repairing a hedge”).], nor grub in the woods, nor cut down trees [Note: [Col. 0519] B has *cedendo* (“while cutting”).], nor work among stones, nor build houses [Note: [Col. 0519] 3 omits the words from *nec domos struere* through *in horto laborent*.]; nor shall they work in the garden [Note: [Col. 0519] B has *laborant* (“they work”); 6, G, and Bal. have *laborare* (“to work”).], nor assemble for lawsuits, nor engage in hunting.

But three kinds of cart-transport may be undertaken on Sunday: military carts, carts carrying provisions [Note: [Col. 0519] G omits *tria carraria opera* (“three cart-works”).], and, if it should happen to be necessary, the conveyance of anyone’s body to burial [Note: [Col. 0519] *hostilia* is corrected in 1 to *hostialia*; in 3 to *ostilicia*; 6 has *hostialia*.].

Women likewise must not perform textile work, nor cut out clothing, nor sew [Note: [Col. 0519] 1* has *consuent* (“they shall sew”).], nor make embroidery [Note: [Col. 0519] The reading *acupictile* is restored by Baluzius from chapter 789. Variants include *acupulae*, corrected to *acupicilae* in 1; *acupiculae* in 1*, 3, 6, and G; *acupicule* in nine manuscripts of Bal.; *acupicula* in B, Par., Met., and Rem.; *acubiculae* in 4; *aucupiculae* in Bal.; *cupiculae* in Camb.; *apicule* in Sang. 1; *apicula* in Pith.; *acupicale* in Norm.; and *aliquapictile* in Sang. 2.], nor have permission to card wool, beat flax, wash clothing in public, or shear sheep [Note: [Col. 0519] 1*, B, Bal., and chapter 789 read *faciant* (“let them do this”); the other manuscripts and nearly all of Bal.’s witnesses read *fiant* (“let these things be done”).], so that the rest of the good [Note: [Col. 0519] This is the reading of our text and twelve of Baluzius’s manuscripts; Bal. has *honor et requies* (“honor and rest”).] may in every way be rendered on the Lord’s Day [Note: [Col. 0519] 4 has *persolvantur* (“may be fulfilled”); G has *persolvat* (“may fulfill”).].

Instead, let them gather from every direction to the church for the solemn celebrations of Mass, and praise God for all the good things he has done for us on that day.

### 76. On the Preaching of Bishops and Priests

It is also your responsibility, beloved and venerable shepherds and rulers of the churches of God, to ensure [Note: [Col. 0519] 3 has *hoc vobis videndum* (“this must be seen by you”); G has *summopere vobis* (“you must take the greatest care”).] that the priests whom you send throughout your dioceses to govern and preach to the people serving God preach rightly [Note: [Col. 0519] 3 has *s. recte praedicent* (“that they preach rightly”).] and honorably. Do not allow anyone to invent and preach to the people new or uncanonical teachings from his own judgment and not according to the sacred Scriptures [Note: [Col. 0519] G omits *non* (“not”).].

You yourselves must also preach honorably and rightly those things that are useful and lead to eternal life [Note: [Col. 0519] B has *ducant* (“lead”) instead of *ducunt* (“lead”).], and instruct others to preach these same things [Note: [Col. 0519] 3, G, and Bal. have *et ipsi praedicent* (“and that they themselves preach them”).].

Above all, this must be preached to everyone generally: that they believe the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit to be one God, omnipotent, eternal, and invisible, who created heaven and earth, the sea, and everything that is in them; and that there is one deity, substance, and majesty [Note: [Col. 0519] The phrase is absent in 3.] in the three persons of the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit.

It must also be preached how the Son of God was incarnate from the Holy Spirit and Mary ever-virgin for the salvation and restoration [Note: [Col. 0519] 6 has *redemptione* (“redemption”).] of the human race; how he suffered, was buried, rose again on the third day, and ascended into heaven; and how he will come again in divine majesty to judge all people according to their own merits [Note: [Col. 0519] G has *et* (“and”) instead of *in* (“in”).]. It must be preached how the wicked, because of their crimes [Note: [Col. 0519] 1** has *secundum* (“according to”) instead of *propter* (“because of”).], will be sent with the devil into eternal fire, while the righteous will enter eternal life with Christ and his holy angels.

It must also be preached diligently that they will receive the resurrection of the dead [Note: [Col. 0519] 3 omits the words from *se* (“themselves”) through *est* (“is”).] [Note: [Col. 0519] Bal., from chapter 789, adds: “so that they may know and believe that in those same bodies they will receive the rewards of their merits.”].

With every care it must be preached to all for which crimes people are consigned [Note: [Col. 0519] 1 has *deponentur* (“will be consigned”).] with the devil to eternal punishment. For we read the apostle saying: “The works of the flesh are manifest: fornication, impurity, debauchery, idolatry, magic, enmity, strife, jealousy, anger, quarrels, dissensions, heresies, sects, envy, murder, drunkenness, revelries, and things like these, which I foretell to you as I foretold them, because those who do such things will not obtain the kingdom of God” [Note: [Col. 0519] The words from *quoniam* through *consequentur* (“because … will obtain”) are absent in B.].

Therefore these same things, which the great preacher of the Church of God named one by one, must be forbidden with every effort, understanding how dreadful is what he said: “Those who do such things will not possess the kingdom of God” [Note: [Col. 0519] 3 and Bal. have *consequentur* (“will obtain”) instead of *possidebunt* (“will possess”).].

With equal earnestness [Note: [Col. 0519] 6 has *studio* (“with zeal”); 1* has *studio et instantia* (“with study and all urgency”).] admonish them concerning love of God and neighbor, faith and hope in God, humility and patience, chastity and continence, kindness and mercy, almsgiving and confession of their sins, and that, according to the Lord’s Prayer, they forgive their debtors their debts, knowing with complete certainty that those who do such things will possess the kingdom of God [Note: [Col. 0519] 3 has: “because those who do such things will not obtain the kingdom of God.”].

We impose this upon your charity with particular diligence because we know that in the last times false teachers will come, as the Lord himself foretold in the Gospel and the apostle Paul attests in his letter to Timothy.

Therefore, beloved, let us prepare ourselves with our whole heart in the knowledge of truth, so that we may be able to resist those who contradict the truth; and, by God’s gracious gift, may the word of God grow, run, and multiply for the advancement of the holy Church of God [Note: [Col. 0519] The words are absent in 3.], for the salvation of our souls, and for the praise and glory of the name [Note: [Col. 0519] The word is absent in 4.] of our Lord Jesus Christ.

Peace to those who preach, grace [Note: [Col. 0519] 3 and B have *gloria* (“glory”).] to those who obey, glory [Note: [Col. 0519] 3 has *laus* (“praise”).] to our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.

### 77. On Church Property

Since, according to the tradition of the holy fathers, we know that the property of the Church is the vows [Note: [Col. 0519] 1 corrects *vota* (“vows”) to *vitam* (“life”); 4 and G have *vitam*; 6 has *vita* (“life”).] of the faithful, the price of sins, and the patrimony of the poor, we wish [Note: [Col. 0521] 3 has *unicuique* (“to each individual”) instead of *cuique* (“to each”).] [Note: [Col. 0521] 1 has *debemus* (“we ought”); 4 has *conservare* (“to preserve”).] not only to preserve for each person what is possessed, but also, with God’s help, to contribute much [Note: [Col. 0521] 4 again has *conservare* (“to preserve”).].

Nevertheless, so that we might completely remove from ecclesiastical persons the suspicion formerly conceived concerning the non-division of that property [Note: [Col. 0521] Add. III, 1 adds *illius ecclesiae* (“of that church”); Colb., Vat. 1, Norm., and Sangall. have *res ecclesiarum* (“the property of the churches”).], we decree that neither in our time, nor in the time of our sons, nor, by God’s dispensation, in the time of our successors who may wish to imitate our will or the example of our ancestors [Note: [Col. 0521] 4 has *voluerunt* (“who wished”).], shall it suffer any division or loss [Note: [Col. 0521] 3, 4, 6, G, and Bal. have *patiantur* (“shall they suffer”).].

[Note: [Col. 0521] Codex 3 adds this chapter after the present chapter, and 3b after chapter 72: “It also seemed good to append what is found in the decrees of Pope Gelasius: that the property of the church and likewise of the diocese should rightly be claimed by the bishops from those by whom it is possessed, which the thirty-year law has enclosed, because the authority of our sons and princes has likewise decreed that no one may bring an action concerning this after thirty years, since the period established by law has excluded it.”]

### 78. On the Election of Bishops

Not ignorant of the sacred canons, and desiring that the holy Church might more freely possess its honor in God’s name [Note: [Col. 0521] 3, B, and eight of Bal.’s manuscripts have *potiatur* (“may possess”); G omits *honore* (“honor”); Vat. 1, Colb., Sang., and Norm. have *iure* (“right”) instead of *honore*.], we have given our assent to the ecclesiastical order, namely, that bishops should be chosen by election of the clergy and people, according to the statutes of the canons, from their own diocese, with all acceptance of persons and gifts removed, on account of the merit of their life and the gift of wisdom [Note: [Col. 0521] 4 has *et ob* (“and on account of”).], so that by example and word they may be able to benefit those subject to them in every way [Note: [Col. 0521] B has *exemplo verbo* (“by the example of the word”); codex 2 adds two chapters here; see above.].

### 79. On the Sayings of the Fathers Collected for the Canonical Profession, Which Had Been Dishonored

Since the canonical profession was being dishonored by many, partly through ignorance [Note: [Col. 0521] 3 omits the remainder after *partim ignorantia* (“partly through ignorance”).] and partly through laziness, we thought it worthwhile, with God’s approval [Note: [Col. 0521] D has *diximus* (“we said”); 1* has *annuntiente* (“with God announcing”).], to gather at the sacred assembly, as from various meadows, by plucking certain blossoming flowers from the sayings of the holy fathers [Note: [Col. 0521] 1* has “as though from various meadows, from various parts”; 3 has *ex patris* (“from the fathers”) and *congerere studuimus et* (“we have endeavored to collect and”); G has *partibus* (“from the parts”); 4, 6, Til., Thu., and Div. also have *partibus*.], into one rule for canons and canonesses, and to hand it over for observance to canons and nuns, so that through it the canonical order might be observed without ambiguity [Note: [Col. 0521] B has *contingere* (“to gather/bring together”) instead of *congerere* (“to collect”).].

And since the sacred assembly praised it so highly that it judged it must be observed down to a single iota [Note: [Col. 0521] 1, 4, 6, and eight manuscripts of Bal. have *ita* (“so”) instead of *iota* (“iota”).], we decree that all living in this profession must hold to it without doubt, and that it must henceforth be observed in every respect by both canons and nuns living canonically [Note: [Col. 0521] 3 has *ea* (“by it”) instead of *eadem* (“in the same profession”).].

### 80. On Distributing Gifts Made to the Church

It has been decreed that whatever is freely given by the faithful to the churches during our reign is to be divided in richer places into two parts for the use of the poor and a third for the stipends of clerics or monks [Note: [Col. 0521] Sang. omits *aut monachorum* (“or monks”).]; in poorer places it is to be divided equally between the clergy and the poor [Note: [Col. 0521] 3 and 3b have *aequo* (“equally/in an equal share”) instead of *aeque* (“equally”); both have *federe* instead of *fore* (“to be”).], unless perhaps the donors have specifically determined how and where it is to be given [Note: [Col. 0521] 3 has *ubi dandum sit* (“where it is to be given”).].

### 81. On the Election of Abbots

Since, with God’s help, we have arranged in part the affairs of monks [Note: [Col. 0521] 3 has *monachorum eligendum* (“of the monks to be chosen”) instead of *Monachorum … causam* (“the affairs of monks”).]—how we have given them permission to elect abbots for themselves from among themselves [Note: [Col. 0521] 3 has *et quotiens* (“and how often”); Vat. 1, 2, Met., and Camb. have *et quomodo* (“and how”); Paris. and Pith. omit the words through *ordinaverimus* (“we have ordered”).], and how we have ordered that they should be able to live peacefully [Note: [Col. 0521] 3 has *quiete* (“quietly”) instead of *quieti* (“peacefully”) and guard their purpose without weariness—we have caused these matters to be carefully recorded in another document, and, so that it might remain valid among our successors and be preserved inviolate, we have confirmed it.

### 82. On the Ordination of Slaves

Concerning the ordination of slaves, who were indiscriminately being advanced everywhere to ecclesiastical orders [Note: [Col. 0521] 4 and 6 have *provehuntur* (“are being advanced”).], it pleased everyone that this matter ought to be brought into agreement with the sacred canons [Note: [Col. 0521] 1* has *concordari* (“that it be brought into agreement”).].

It was therefore decreed [Note: [Col. 0521] G, Reg., Sang., Norm., Trec., Vat. 1, and Bal. have *unde* (“therefore”) instead of *et* (“and”).] that henceforth no bishop presume to advance them to sacred orders [Note: [Col. 0521] 3 has *gradus* (“ranks”) instead of *ordines* (“orders”)], unless they have first obtained freedom from their own masters.

If any slave, fleeing from or hiding from his master, or using witnesses hired or bribed by payment, or by any other trick or fraud, should reach ecclesiastical orders, it is decreed that he be deposed and that his master receive him.

If, however, a grandfather or father, migrating from one homeland to another [Note: [Col. 0521] Reg., Trec., and Bal. have *aliqua patria* (“some homeland”).], fathered a son in the same province, and that son was raised there and promoted to ecclesiastical orders [Note: [Col. 0521] 4 omits *et* (“and”).], without knowing [Note: [Col. 0521] B, Rem., Pith., and Par. have *ignoratum fuerit* (“and it was unknown”) instead of *ignoraverit* (“he did not know”).] that he was a slave, and afterward his master came and legally claimed him [Note: [Col. 0521] 1 has *quisierit* (“claimed”); 4 has a longer variant: “afterward the master of that man came and, if he wished to grant him freedom …,” but the remainder is absent.], it is decreed that, if his master wishes to grant him freedom, he remain in his rank; but if the master wishes to drag him from the lord’s camp by the chain of slavery, he shall lose his rank [Note: [Col. 0522] The text breaks here into a new column.], because a person remaining in a servile condition cannot exercise the dignity of the priesthood in accordance with the sacred orders.

Concerning their property or personal holdings [Note: [Col. 0521] 4 and G have *peculiari* (“personal property”); HLD has *peculio* (“property”).]—those who are granted freedom by their own masters so that they may lawfully be promoted to ecclesiastical orders—it has been decreed that it remain in the power of the masters whether they wish to grant those things to them or claim them for themselves [Note: [Col. 0521] 1* has *vellint* (“wish”).].

For the rest, if he acquires anything after ordination [Note: [Col. 0521] 6 and B have *adquisierint* (“if they acquire”).], the rule established in the canons concerning consecrated persons who possess nothing shall be observed [Note: [Col. 0521] 1* begins a new chapter here, titled “From the Council of Carthage.”].

Concerning the slaves of churches, it has been decreed by common agreement that the archbishops established in each province should possess our authority, and their suffragans a copy of it [Note: [Col. 0521] The words *exemplar illius* (“a copy of it”) are absent in 3.].

Whenever someone useful from the household of the church is found to be ordained [Note: [Col. 0523] 3 has *ordinatus* (“ordained”) instead of *ordinandus* (“to be ordained”).], the authority itself must be read before the people in the ambo, and before priests or faithful laymen before the horn of the altar, as it is contained in our authority [Note: [Col. 0523] The words from *et coram* through *sacerdotibus* are absent in 3 and 4.]; after every trickery has been removed, he must receive freedom [Note: [Col. 0523] 4 has *consequantur* (“they must receive freedom”).], and only then may he be promoted to ecclesiastical orders [Note: [Col. 0523] 1* and 4 have *promoveantur* (“they may be promoted”).].

The same procedure must be followed concerning those whom laymen wish to promote from the households of churches to sacred orders [Note: [Col. 0523] 1* has *laicos* (“laymen”) instead of *laici* (“laymen”).]. The same form must also be observed concerning those whom the superiors of canons or monks request to be ordained [Note: [Col. 0523] 4 omits *quos* (“whom”) and *monachorum* (“of monks”).].

### 83. From Whom Property Must Not Be Accepted

It has been decreed that no ecclesiastical person henceforth presume to accept property from persons whose children or relatives might, through this ill-considered offering, be disinherited of their own property [Note: [Col. 0523] 3 has *rebus propriis* (“their own possessions”); 4 and 6 have *rem propriam* (“their own property”); B, Camb., Rem., Norm., Par., and Pith. have *exhereditari* (“be disinherited”).].

If anyone thereafter attempts to do this, he must in every way be struck down by synodal or imperial judgment [Note: [Col. 0523] 3 has *a synodo* (“by a synod”) instead of *a synodali* (“by synodal”).].

[Note: [Col. 0523] The final sentence of this chapter is taken from chapter 8 of the Aachen capitulary above, column 398, while all the preceding material had been copied from chapter 7. It is therefore clear that Ansegisus, deceived by the similarity of the wording, omitted the final sentence of chapter 7 and most of chapter 8 and compressed the two chapters into one. Only the Divionensis, Rivipullensis, and Normannicus codices present both chapters. That this is a fault of Ansegisus, not of the copyists, is evident from the Worms capitulary of 829, chapter 5, in which Book I, chapter 157, together with this number, is copied.]

### 84. On Appointing Priests

It has been decreed that priests may neither be appointed nor expelled in any churches without the authority or consent of the bishops.

If laymen offer bishops clerics of worthy life and teaching to be consecrated and appointed in their churches [Note: [Col. 0523] *episcopis* (“to bishops”) is abbreviated differently in 1 and B.], the bishops must not reject them on any pretext.

### 85. On the Manses of Each Church

It has been decreed that one complete manse be assigned to each church without any other service [Note: [Col. 0523] 1 omits *alio* (“other”); 3 has *ullo* (“any”); B has *aliquo* (“some”).].

The priests appointed to them must perform no service from the tithes, the offerings of the faithful, the houses, the courtyards or gardens situated beside the church, or the aforesaid manse, except ecclesiastical service.

If they possess anything more, they must render from it the service owed to their lords.

### 86. On the Priests of Each Church

It has been decreed, once this has been fulfilled, that each church should have its own priest wherever the bishop, providing for it, permits this to be possible [Note: [Col. 0523] This entire chapter is omitted in G, Sang. 1, Thu., and Colb.].

### 87. On New Villages and Churches Newly Established in Them

It has been decreed concerning new villages and churches newly established in them [Note: [Col. 0523] 3 places this chapter after the following one.] that tithes from those villages be given to those same churches [Note: [Col. 0523] The words are absent in 3.].

### 88. On Sacred Church Vessels Given as Pledges

Concerning the sacred vessels of the church which we have learned are given as pledges by some people in certain places [Note: [Col. 0523] 4 has *vasibus* (“vessels”) instead of *vasis*.], it has been forbidden that anyone presume henceforth to do this, except when compelled by the sole necessity of ransoming captives.

### 89. On Destroyed Churches, and on Ninths and Tithes

Concerning destroyed churches [Note: [Col. 0523] 3 has *constructis* (“constructed”) instead of *destructis* (“destroyed”).], ninths [Note: [Col. 0523] G consistently has *annonis* (“annual levies”) instead of *nonis* (“ninths”) throughout Ansegisus and Benedictus.] and tithes, and canonical cloisters, we have noted below in other chapters how we have decided that they should be established and ordered [Note: [Col. 0523] G omits *qualiter* (“how”).].

### 90. On the Honor of Churches

Likewise, concerning the honor of churches, and how, with God’s help, it may flourish as far as lies within us [Note: [Col. 0523] G has *viget* (“it flourishes”).], it is likewise understood to have been inserted in the chapters noted below [Note: [Col. 0523] 3 omits the words concerning the honor of churches; B has only *honor* (“honor”).].

### 91. On the Bishops of Italy

Concerning the bishops established in Lombardy [Note: [Col. 0523] 3 has “the bishops of Italy who …”], who were accustomed to receive or demand from those whom they ordained oaths and gifts contrary to divine and canonical authority [Note: [Col. 0523] 4 has *solliciti* (“concerned”) instead of *soliti* (“accustomed”).], it has been absolutely forbidden that this happen any longer, because, according to the sacred canons, both parties who do such things ought to be cast down from their proper rank [Note: [Col. 0523] 1* has *a gradu* (“from the rank”); 4 has *deici* (“be cast down”).].

### 92. On Priests Who Keep Women in Their Houses

It has been decreed by the bishops concerning priests who indiscriminately permit women to live with them and, on account of this, are marked by suspicion of a bad reputation, that if, after being admonished, they do not correct themselves, they are to be struck as despisers of the sacred canons by canonical punishment.

### 93. On Priests Who Used to Come for Chrism on Maundy Thursday

Concerning priests who used to come to the cities to receive chrism on the Lord’s Supper [Note: [Col. 0523] G omits *ad civitates* (“to the cities”).], it has been decreed that, from among those who live far away, one be chosen by the bishop from every eight or ten [Note: [Col. 0523] 3b has *de octo vel decem milibus* (“from eight or ten thousand”); 1* has *de decem* (“from ten”).] miles, to carry the chrism he has received carefully to himself and his companions.

Those who live no farther than four or five miles from the city should come in person, as usual, to receive the chrism.

For the sake of learning [Note: [Col. 0523] 4 and 6 have *dicendi gratia* (“for the sake of speaking”); G has *verbi gratia* (“for the sake of the word”).], however, they should be summoned to the cities at another time, not during Lent.

### 94. On the Preaching and Confirmation of Bishops

So that bishops would not become a burden to the people under the pretext of preaching or confirmation, after being admonished by us they promised that henceforth they would avoid this [Note: [Col. 0523] The words are absent in 1, 6, and G.] and would perform their ministry at whatever time the opportunity was given [Note: [Col. 0523] 1 and 1* originally had *dabatur* (“was given”), corrected to *dabitur* (“is given”); 3 and the other manuscripts have *dabatur*.], so that their journey, insofar as it lay within them [Note: [Col. 0523] 1 originally had *erat* (“was”), corrected to *erit* (“will be”).], would not be inconvenient or burdensome to those whom they can and ought to benefit [Note: [Col. 0523] 1 originally had *possunt* (“can”); G has *possint et debent* (“may and ought”).] [Note: [Col. 0523] 3 has “so that they are not troublesome or burdensome”; B, Norm., Pith., and Par. have “their visitation.”].

### 95. On Tonsuring Boys and Veiling Girls

It is absolutely forbidden that boys be tonsured without their parents’ consent or that girls be veiled.

Whoever attempts to do this [Note: [Col. 0525] 4 has “whoever attempts this must be compelled.”] must be compelled to pay the fine contained in the chapters of the secular law established by us.

### 96. Concerning Women Who Lose Their Husbands

Concerning women who lose their husbands, it is pleasing that they should not, as hitherto, veil themselves indiscriminately [Note: [Col. 0525] *velentur* (“be veiled”), G.], but that they should wait thirty days after the death [Note: [Col. 0525] *discessum* (“departure”), 3.] of their husband, and after the thirtieth day, with the advice of their bishop—or, if the bishop is absent, with the advice of their other religious priests, their relatives, and their friends—choose what they ought to choose. And because [Note: [Col. 0525] *qui* corrected to *quia*, 1; “because the holy assembly,” 1.] we were asked by the holy assembly [Note: [Col. 0525] *rogat et hi* (“and they ask”), 3; *rogati sumus ut* (“we were asked that”), 1*, Bell., B., Pith., Norm., Rem., Par.] that those performing public penance [Note: [Col. 0525] G. reads *gerunt … amittunt* (“are performing … are losing”), rather than the past tenses.] and women who had lost their husbands [Col. 0525B] should be protected, by our authority [Note: [Col. 0525] *nostram auctoritatem* (“our authority”), B.], until they should deliberate what they ought to do, we have decreed that special chapters concerning them be composed and inserted into the chapters of the secular law [Note: [Col. 0525] *tuerentur* (“should be protected”); *uerentur*, 1; *tueantur* (“should be protected”), G.; 4 has a correction from *tuerentur*. “chapters concerning women and laymen” are absent in 4.].

### 97. Concerning Abducted Women and Their Abductors

Although we had decreed specifically what those who thereafter attempted to commit this crime ought to suffer, nevertheless, concerning abducted women and their abductors, we have judged it necessary to insert here what the sacred canons prescribe [Note: [Col. 0525] *praecipiant* (“prescribe”), 1*, 3, B.], so that it may be clear to everyone how great an evil this is, and so that, constrained not only by human but also by divine authority, all may henceforth avoid this evil [Note: [Col. 0525] *caveant* (“may avoid”), 1; *ab omnibus caveatur* (“may be avoided by all”), B., G., Norm., Rem., Par., Bal.].

### 98. Concerning Abducted Girls Who Are Not Yet Betrothed

Concerning girls who have been abducted and are not yet betrothed, it is stated as follows in the Council of Chalcedon, where 630 fathers were present [Note: [Col. 0525] “330,” 3; “two hundred thirty,” 4.], in chapter 38 [Note: [Col. 0525] “27,” 4; “28,” Rivip.]:

“The holy synod decreed that those who abduct girls under the pretext of living together, and those who cooperate with or connive at the abductors, if they are clerics, shall be removed from their proper rank; but if they are laymen, they shall be anathematized.”

By these words it is plainly understood how the perpetrators of this evil are to be condemned, since participants and those who connive are struck with so great an anathema [Note: [Col. 0525] absent in 1, 1*, Hld.], and [Note: [Col. 0525] 1* adds *et quod* (“and that”).], in accordance with canonical authority, they can in no way lawfully claim as wives for themselves those who have been abducted [Note: [Col. 0525] *possit* (“can”), 1.].

### 99. Concerning Betrothed Girls Abducted by Others

Concerning betrothed girls who have subsequently been abducted by others, it is read as follows in the Council of Ancyra [Note: [Col. 0525] *ancyrano*, G.], chapter ten:

“It was decided that betrothed girls who have later been abducted by others should be rescued and restored to those to whom they had previously been betrothed [Note: [Col. 0525] *fuerint* (“had been”), 1, 1*, B.; *fuerunt*, G., Hld.], even if it is established that violence was inflicted upon them by the abductors.”

Therefore it was decreed by the holy assembly that the abductor be punished with public penance. But if the betrothed man does not wish to receive the abducted woman [Note: [Col. 0525] *raptae* (“of the abducted woman”), 1*, B., Bal.; Bal. reads “if the fiancé does not wish to receive her”], and she did not consent to the same crime [Note: [Col. 0525] *eiusdem* (“the same”), 1; *eodem*, G., Hld.; *criminis*, B.], she is not to be denied permission to marry another. But if she too consented, she shall be subject to the same sentence. If thereafter they presume to join themselves to each other, let both be anathematized [Note: [Col. 0525] The words following “but if” are absent in 3; 3 instead reads: “if he should presume to join himself to her”; B.: “if he should presume to join himself to her.”].

### 100. Concerning Those Who Join Themselves to Virgins Dedicated to God

Concerning those who join themselves to sacred virgins, the following is contained in the decrees of Pope Gelasius, chapter 20 [Note: [Col. 0525] 3 has *ita de incestis* (“thus concerning incestuous persons”); “30,” 4, 6, Reg., Bal.; B. inserts this chapter here, although it does not include it in the table of contents; Pith., Par., Norm., and Rem. likewise insert it here.]:

“We have learned that certain men rashly join themselves to sacred virgins and, after their dedication to God, contract incestuous and sacrilegious unions with them. It is therefore just that they be immediately expelled from holy communion, and, unless they perform public and approved penance, that they not be received at all [Note: [Col. 0525] *recipere* (“to receive”), 3; *recipiantur* (“be received”), 4; *recipit* (“receives”), B.]; or [Note: [Col. 0525] 3 reads *at* (“but”); 4 omits the introductory word.] at least that the viaticum not be denied them when they are departing from this world, provided that they have repented. But if those who unite themselves with sacred virgins are punished so severely, how much more severely must those be punished who abduct them [Note: [Col. 0525] 4 places “those who abduct them” before “how much more severely”?]. Therefore, as has been stated above, it is necessary that, through the strictness of divine or human authority, this evil be uprooted completely by all who remain within the Christian religion.”

### 101. Concerning the Time at Which Girls Are to Be Veiled

But lest girls be veiled indiscriminately, we have also decided to set forth here from the sacred canons what is to be observed concerning the time for veiling girls. In the African Council [Note: [Col. 0525] 1* reads *cartaginensi* (“Carthaginian”).], chapter 16, it is contained that they are not to be consecrated before the age of twenty-five. Likewise, in the same council, chapter 93 [Note: [Col. 0525] “the ninetieth,” G.], the following is contained concerning the veiling of virgins:

“It was likewise decided that any bishop who, because virginal chastity is endangered, fears either a powerful suitor or an abductor, or who veils—or has veiled—a virgin before twenty-five years of age because she is troubled by some peril of death lest she die unveiled, at the demand either of her parents or of those to whose care she belongs, shall not be prejudiced by the council’s statute concerning that number of years [Note: [Col. 0525] *cum* (“when/with”), and 3, 4, 6, B. have the abbreviated *c. et v.*; G. reads *et cum* (“and when”); 3 has “fifteen” for “twenty-five”; *periculo* (“danger”), 3; *consecratio* (“consecration”), 4, G.].”

From this it is gathered that, according to the earlier sanction, virgins are properly to be consecrated in the twenty-fifth year of their age [Note: [Col. 0525] *ritae* (“properly”), G.]. But if the aforesaid necessities compel this to be done earlier, it cannot bring any prejudice to the bishop’s consecration [Note: [Col. 0525] Bal. adds here three chapters taken from the capitularies of Lothar above.].

### 102. Concerning the Trial by the Holy Cross Not to Be Performed

It has been decreed that henceforth no one presume to perform any trial by the cross [Note: [Col. 0525] 1* reads *qualibet examinatione cruces* (“any trial of the cross”); B. and the other manuscripts of this family add “holy.”], lest the Passion of Christ [Note: [Col. 0525] *passionem* (“Passion”), 4, 6.], which is glorification [Note: [Col. 0525] 1 corrects the reading to “the Passion which is glorification”; Vat., Met., Div., Bellov., Camb., Pal., Til., Rem., B., Pith., Par., Norm., and G. read “the Passion, not glorification”; 1* reads “the Passion and glorification of rashness.”], be held in contempt through anyone’s rashness [Col. 0526D].

### 103. Concerning the Proclamation of the Nourishment of the Divine Word

Bishops [Note: [Col. 0525] *eps*, 1*, B.; Bal. reads *epos monemus ut* (“we admonish bishops that …”).], whether personally or through deputies, are diligently to proclaim to the peoples the nourishment of the divine word [Col. 0527A] [Note: [Col. 0527] *sedule* (“diligently”), 3, 4; *scedule*, B.; *adnuntiet* (“let him proclaim”), 1*.]. For, as blessed Gregory says, a priest arouses against himself the anger of the hidden Judge if he goes about without the sound of preaching.

And we earnestly admonished them to nourish the clergy entrusted to them in sobriety and chastity [Note: [Col. 0527] *clericum* (“cleric”), B.; *ipsi clerum* (“the clergy themselves”), Bal.] and to instruct them in the divine offices, so that those who could properly be promoted to the sacred ecclesiastical orders might be formed accordingly [Note: [Col. 0527] *nutriant … imbuant … possint* (“let them nourish … instruct … be able”), 1*, 3, B.].

They are also to take care that the presbyters have a well-corrected missal [Note: [Col. 0527] *missarium*, 1, 6; *missarum*, Hld.], lectionary, and other books necessary to them; that, as far as their strength permits, they repair the churches belonging to them that have fallen into ruin [Note: [Col. 0527] *destructas sibi pertinentes* (“ruined and belonging to them”), 1*, 4, 6, B.]; and that they carefully instruct widows, teaching them how they ought to conduct themselves according to apostolic authority [Note: [Col. 0527] *edoceantur* (“may be instructed”), G.].

They are also to eradicate the superstitions that some people practice in certain places at the funerals of the dead; by the example of their innocence, to encourage others to live well [Note: [Col. 0527] “others” is absent in 4.]; and, insofar as the Lord assists them [Note: [Col. 0527] *iutaverit*, 6; *iuverit* (“assists”), 1* corrected, B., Bal.], to strive with all their strength to provide for all ecclesiastical affairs. And so that they may carry this out more freely, we desire by every means to give them assistance, insofar as the Lord grants us the ability [Note: [Col. 0527] “the Lord” is absent in 1, 3; 1* omits *posse* (“ability”).].

### 104. Concerning Incestuous Marriages and Churches to Be Divided

We have judged it worthy to defer certain chapters—such as those concerning incestuous marriages [Note: [Col. 0527] absent in G.]; churches that are divided among co-heirs and thereby deprived of their proper dignity; churches whose resources have been excessively reduced [Note: [Col. 0527] *adnuntiate*, 1; *adunatae*, 4, 6; *annullatae*, G., Colb., Sang.]; and, indeed, those matters that have recently been taken away from certain churches under the compulsion of necessity [Note: [Col. 0527] *certae* (“certain”), B.]—as well as any other matters, whether ecclesiastical or public, that deserve correction but which, because of the shortness of time, we were unable to accomplish, until, with the Lord’s favor, the opportunity to define them is granted to us through the counsel of the faithful [Note: [Col. 0527] *consulta* (“having consulted”), 1, 3, and 1*; here corrected to *consultu* (“through counsel”).].

But “things found”—the transmitted *inventa vero ut* is syntactically awkward [Note: [Col. 0527] 1 has *interim* (“meanwhile”) in the margin]—so that, with God’s help, they may achieve their effect over time, we have judged should be inserted here [Note: [Col. 0527] G. and Pithoeus’s edition read: “we wish to confirm in writing the matters already amended, corrected, and restored.”].

### 105. Concerning Scribes

Concerning scribes: let each of them write without error [Note: [Col. 0527] G., Vat., 1, Sang., and Golb. read: “We command that all scribes …”].

### 106. Concerning Male and Female Serfs

Concerning male and female serfs: let them not be tonsured or veiled beyond the prescribed measure, and let sufficient provision be made for them there [Note: [Col. 0527] *ubi* (“where”), 3, 4.] so that the estates may not be left deserted [Note: [Col. 0527] *dissolutae* (“dissolved”), B.].

### 107. Concerning Gatherings

Concerning unnecessary gatherings: let them in no way take place; but let him gather as many as he can advise [Note: [Col. 0527] *quantos* (“as many [masculine]”), 3, B., N., Par.; *dari* (“to be given”), B., N., Rem., Pith.; Bal. reads “let whoever can give counsel gather them”; *congregate* (“gather”), B., Norm., Par., Rem., Pith.].

### 108. Concerning Those Who Ring [the Bell]

Concerning those who are not made *pulsati* (“rung/called”) according to the rule [Note: [Col. 0527] 3 omits “who are not made”; 4 reads *sunt* (“are”)], let them henceforth be corrected and *pulsent* (“ring/call”) according to the rule [Note: [Col. 0527] *pulsentur* (“be rung/called”), 3, B., Bal.].

### 109. Concerning Infant Girls and When They Are to Be Veiled

Let girls of infant age [Note: [Col. 0527] “of girlhood,” G., Vat., 1, Sang., Colb.] not be veiled before they know how to choose what they want [Note: [Col. 0527] Bal., from Sang., Thun., Palat., Colb., and Rem., adds “and let them be summoned,” evidently drawn from the preceding chapter.], without prejudice to canonical authority.

### 110. Concerning Superiors of Monks

Let laymen not be superiors of monks within monasteries; and let archdeacons not be laymen [Note: [Col. 0527] *nec* (“nor”), 3, B., Bal.].

### 111. Concerning Those Guilty of Incest

Concerning those guilty of incest: let them be examined canonically, and let some not be released and others constrained on account of anyone’s friendship [Note: [Col. 0527] 3 reads *ne* (“nor”) for *nec* (“and not”); the words “some are released, others are constrained” are absent in B.].

### 112. Concerning Famine, Calamity, and Pestilence, Should They Occur

If famine, calamity, pestilence [Note: [Col. 0527] *pestilentiae* (“of pestilence”), 6.] and irregularity of the weather, or any other kind of tribulation should occur, let no one await an edict of ours, but let God’s mercy immediately be entreated. And in the present year, because of the scarcity caused by famine [Col. 0528B], let each person assist his own people as he is able, and let him not sell his grain too dearly [Note: [Col. 0527] *ut* (“so that”), 1*.]. And let no foodstuff be sold outside our empire [Note: [Col. 0527] *aliquod* (“anything”), 1*.] [Note: [Col. 0527] *alimonii* (“of food”), G.].

### 113. Concerning Fugitive Clerics and Laymen

Concerning fugitive clerics or laymen, and also women: let the rule be observed as we prescribed in another capitulary [Note: [Col. 0527] *praecipimus* (“we prescribe”), 1, Hld.].

### 114. Concerning Free Men Who Give Themselves to the Service of God

Concerning free men who wish to give themselves to the service of God [Note: [Col. 0527] G. reads: “we prescribe that those who wish …”]: let them not do this before first requesting permission from us. This is because we have heard that some of them did so not so much out of devotion as in order to escape military service or another royal obligation [Note: [Col. 0527] *confunctione*, 6.], while we have heard that others were deceived for the sake of greed by those who coveted their property. For this reason we prohibit it from being done.

### 115. Concerning the Oppression of the Poor

Concerning the oppression of poor free men [Note: [Col. 0527] This phrase is absent in Vat., Thu., Sang.]: let them not be oppressed by more powerful persons through any fraudulent device contrary to justice, so that they are compelled to sell or surrender their property. For this reason we have spoken of free men both above and here, lest perhaps their parents be disinherited contrary to justice [Note: [Col. 0527] *exhereditati* (“disinherited”), 3, B.; also 1*, but corrected here.], royal service be diminished, and the heirs themselves, because of want, become beggars, robbers, or wrongdoers [Note: [Col. 0527] *mendiciles* (“beggars”), 1, 3.].

And let them not be summoned so frequently to hearings except as we prescribed in another capitulary [Note: [Col. 0527] *praecipimus* (“we prescribe”), 1, B.]; let that rule be observed [Note: [Col. 0527] Riv., Sang., and Colb. add: “but let it by all means be observed thus.”].

### 116. Concerning Envoys Sent through Cities and Monasteries

Let envoys sent through each city and through monasteries of men and girls inspect how and in what condition the buildings of the churches and the ornaments of the church appear to have been repaired or restored [Col. 0528D]. Let them also diligently inquire into the conduct of each person [Note: [Col. 0527] *conversione* (“conversion”), G.] and how well they have carried out what we commanded concerning their reading and singing and the other disciplines belonging to the order of ecclesiastical rule [Col. 0529A].

### 117. Concerning Ecclesiastical Treasures

Let each bishop, abbot, and abbess [Note: [Col. 0529] “or abbot,” 1*.] carefully inspect the ecclesiastical treasures, lest through the dishonesty or negligence of the custodians anything of the gems, vessels, or any other remaining treasure [Note: [Col. 0529] absent in 4.] be lost. For it has been reported to us that Jewish merchants and others boast that they can buy from them whatever pleases them [Note: [Col. 0529] *placent* (“they please”), 3.].

### 118. Concerning Wandering Beggars

Concerning beggars who wander throughout the lands: we wish each of our faithful to support his own poor person [Note: [Col. 0529] *suum* (“his own”) is absent in 3.] from his benefice or from his own household [Note: [Col. 0529] *proprio* (“his own”), 1.] and not allow him to go anywhere begging [Col. 0529B] [Note: [Col. 0529] “for the purpose of begging,” 1; “to beg,” 6, G.; *mendicatum*, Hld.; 1* reads “to wander about begging.”]. Wherever such people are found, let them work with their hands for themselves [Note: [Col. 0529] “so that they work with their hands for themselves,” 4, B.; “so that they work for themselves,” 1*.], and let no one presume to give them anything [Note: [Col. 0529] *nullusque* (“and no one”), 3.].

### 119. Concerning Usury

Usury is when more is demanded than is given: for example, if you give ten solidi and demand more; or if you give a measure of wine or grain and again demand something additional [Note: [Col. 0529] *exieris*, 1, 6.].

### 120. Concerning Desire in the Good Sense

Desire can be understood in a good sense and in a bad sense. In the good sense, according to the Apostle: “I desire to depart and to be with Christ.” And in the psalm: “My soul has desired the courts of the Lord.”

### 121. Likewise Concerning Desire in the Bad Sense

Desire is understood in the bad sense when someone wishes unjustly and excessively to seek any possessions, according to Solomon: “Do not pursue your desires” [Col. 0529C].

### 122. Likewise Concerning Greed

Greed is desiring the possessions of others and, once they have been acquired, giving nothing to anyone. And, according to the Apostle, it is the root of all evils.

### 123. Concerning Dishonest Profits

Those practice dishonest profit who, through various deceptions [Note: [Col. 0529] “greedy dealings,” 4, 6.], strive dishonestly [Note: [Col. 0529] *iniuste* (“unjustly”), G.] to gather any possessions for the sake of profit.

### 124. Concerning Interest

Interest is when someone lends something [Note: [Col. 0529] 3b. reads: “interest is what is lent.”]. Just interest is when he demands no more than he lent [Note: [Col. 0529] 3b. reads: “when nothing more is demanded than what is given.”] [Note: [Col. 0529] *praestat* (“he lends”), 3, G.].

### 125. Concerning Buying at Harvest-Time for the Sake of Greed and Dishonest Profit

Whoever, at harvest time or vintage time, buys grain or wine not out of necessity but because of greed—for example, buys one measure for two denarii and stores it until it can be sold for four or six denarii, or more [Note: [Col. 0529] “seven,” 3.]—we call this dishonest profit. If he buys it out of necessity, so that he may keep some for himself and give some to others [Note: [Col. 0529] *quod* (“which”), 4.], we call it commerce.

### 126. Concerning What Is to Be Done if There Is Famine in Many Places

We have therefore considered that a severe famine appears to exist in many places. Let all bishops, abbots, abbesses, nobles, counts, household officials, and all the faithful [Note: [Col. 0529] *et* (“and”) is absent in G.; *cuncti* (“all”) is also absent in G.] who appear to hold royal benefices, whether from ecclesiastical property or from other goods [Note: [Col. 0529] “goods,” Bal.], cause each person to feed his household from his benefice and to support his own household from his own property.

If, by God’s gift, he has grain remaining for himself and his household, whether in his benefice or in his allod [Note: [Col. 0529] “grain elsewhere,” 1*.], and wishes to sell it, let him not sell it for more than two denarii for a measure of oats [Note: [Col. 0529] G. and Bal. read “against two denarii”; 3: “for two denarii.”], three denarii for a measure of barley [Note: [Col. 0529] *modio* (“by/for a measure”), G.] [Note: [Col. 0529] *ordeatio*, B.; *hordea*, Bal.], four denarii for one measure of rye [Note: [Col. 0529] *sigilo*, 1*, 3, B., Bal.; *sigilla*, 4; *sigula*, G.; *siligine*, Hld.; *contra* (“against/for”) is absent in 1.], and six denarii for one measure of prepared wheat [Note: [Col. 0529] *comparat* (“he buys”), 1.]. Let the measure itself be the one that has been established for everyone to possess. And let everyone have an equal measure and equal measures.

### 127. Concerning How Synods Are to Be Held

Let a synod be held twice each year.

### 128. Concerning Metropolitan Bishops

Let no province in any way be divided between two metropolitan bishops [Note: [Col. 0529] “two metropolitan bishops,” 3.].

### 129. Concerning How Many Bishops There Should Be in One City

Let there not be two bishops in one city.

### 130. Concerning the Ordination of Bishops

The ordinations of bishops ought not to be delayed for long.

### 131. Concerning the Stability of Bishops and Clerics

Let a bishop not pass from one place to another without a decree of the bishops, nor a cleric without the command of his bishop.

### 132. Concerning the Communion of the Faithful

Let all the faithful receive communion and remain through the Mass to the end without any further supplication [Note: [Col. 0529] “without any further preaching,” 4, 6.] [Col. 0530C].

### 133. The Canons of Saint Sylvester and 280 Bishops Concerning Presbyters, Deacons, and the Rest of the Clergy

[Note: [Col. 0529] “284,” 1*, G. All of this is absent in 3, 4, 6, B., and Bal.; 1* places it after “clergy”; G. includes it here and in the text.]

He established these ranks in the midst of the synod [Note: [Col. 0529] “in the synodal assembly,” 6; “Saint Sylvester established these synodal ranks,” 4, 3b.], so that no presbyter should bring any accusation against a bishop, no deacon against a presbyter, no subdeacon against a deacon [Note: [Col. 0529] *diaconem* (“deacon”), 3.], no acolyte against a subdeacon, no exorcist against an acolyte, no lector against an exorcist, and no doorkeeper against a lector [Note: [Col. 0529] The words from “no acolyte against a subdeacon” through “no doorkeeper against a lector” are absent in 3.].

And a prelate shall not be condemned without seventy-two witnesses [Note: [Col. 0529] Bal. reads “unless there are”]. Nor shall the supreme prelate be judged by anyone, since it is written: “The disciple is not above the teacher” [Col. 0530D] [Note: [Col. 0529] “Is not the disciple …?”, B.].

A presbyter, however, shall not be condemned without forty-four testimonies [Note: [Col. 0529] *testimoniis* (“testimonies”), Bal.]. A deacon established in the rank of the city of Rome shall not be condemned without thirty-seven [Note: [Col. 0529] “without thirty-three testimonies,” 3, 3b.]. For a subdeacon, acolyte, exorcist, or lector, the transmitted clause is grammatically defective: *nisi, sicut scriptum est, in septem testimoniis filios habentes et uxores et omnino Christum praedicantes*—“unless/except, as it is written, [having] children and wives and altogether preaching Christ, in seven testimonies.” It is preserved here without supplying a missing rule [Note: [Col. 0529] “seventeen,” 1*; [Col. 0531A] *testibus* (“witnesses”), 4.]. Thus the mystical truth is given.

### 134. Concerning Refuge in a Church

If anyone takes refuge in a church, let him have peace in the atrium of that church, and let it not be necessary for him to enter the church. Let no one presume to drag him out of there by force. But let him be permitted to confess what he has done, and from there let him be brought out into public for examination by the hands of good men.

### 135. Concerning Those Who Wish to Give Property to the House of God

Whoever wishes to give his property to the house of God for the sake of his soul [Note: [Col. 0531] *voluerint* (“wish”), 1.] shall make the gift at home before lawful witnesses. Gifts made on campaign, concerning which there is no dispute, shall remain valid.

But if someone has given his property to another and has departed on campaign, and the person to whom the property was given dies in the meantime, the donor, when he returns, shall recover his property after producing the witnesses before whom the gift was made [Note: [Col. 0531] 3 reads *tradiderint* (“have given”); 1* has *r. suas dedit* (“gave his things”); *accipiat* (“receive”), 4.]. But if the donor himself has also died, his lawful heirs shall recover the property given [Note: [Col. 0531] *tres* (“three”), 4.].

### 136. Concerning the Ordination of Presbyters

Let presbyters not be ordained before they have been examined. And let excommunications not be imposed indiscriminately and without cause.

### 137. Concerning the Conversion of a Free Man

Let a free man who has laid aside his hair in a regular monastery and has assigned his property there firmly keep the promise he made according to the rule [Note: [Col. 0531] Bal. reads: “let him be bound by the promise made according to the rule.”].

### 138. Concerning Not Compelling Anyone to Drink

Let no one [Note: [Col. 0531] *neminem* (“no one,” accusative), 1*.] be permitted to compel another to drink [Note: [Col. 0531] The editions of Til. and Pith. add: “except as much as is sufficient.”].

### 139. Concerning Markets

Let no market be held anywhere on the Lord’s Day [Note: [Col. 0531] 1* and 6 combine this chapter with the preceding one, reading *et* (“and”) for *ut*; 3 reads *mercatum* (“market”) and *fiat* (“be done/held”).].

### 140. Concerning Presbyters and How They Are to Obtain Entry into a Church

Let no presbyter give an *exenia* [a gift or offering] upon entering a church [Note: [Col. 0531] *exenia*, with the *e* erased, 1*, 2, 2b, 3; *excenia*, 6.].

### 141. Concerning Who May Establish Presbyters in Churches

Let no layman presume to install or expel a presbyter in a church [Note: [Col. 0531] *eclesiam*, 3, 4, G.; G. reads “admit”; B. omits “install or expel”], except with the consent of the bishop.

### 142. Concerning Honor to Be Given for Churches

Let bishops make provision concerning what honor presbyters are to render for the elder churches [Note: [Col. 0531] “their own churches,” 1*, 3.].

### 143. Concerning the Distribution of Tithes

Let tithes be under the authority of the bishop [Note: [Col. 0531] absent in 5.], as to how they are to be distributed by the presbyters.

### 144. Concerning Churches and Altars

Let churches and altars be constructed better [Note: [Col. 0531] *constituantur* (“be established”), 1*. Vat. and 1 read: “let them be better maintained by the presbyters.”]. Let no presbyter presume to place grain or hay in a church [Note: [Col. 0531] *eclesiam*, 4, G.].

### 145. Concerning Churches and Altars of Doubtful Consecration

Let churches or altars whose consecration is doubtful [Note: [Col. 0531] *ambigua* (“doubtful”), B.; this chapter is absent in G.] be consecrated [Note: [Col. 0531] *de* is absent in 3.].

### 146. Concerning Preparing Linens for Altars

Let presbyters preach throughout their parishes [Note: [Col. 0531] *barrochiis*, consistently; “their own,” 5.] to women that they should prepare linens for the altars [Note: [Col. 0531] “on the altars,” Met.; 5 reads *praedicant* (“they preach”).].

### 147. Concerning the Parishioners of Another Presbytery [Note: [Col. 0531] This heading is absent in 5.]

Let no presbyter receive the parishioner of another presbyter [Note: [Col. 0531] *parrochia* (“parish”), 3; *parrochiam*, 4.] at Mass, unless he is traveling or has a hearing there [Note: [Col. 0531] 1* omits “or the following words through ‘nor the tithe’ at the end of the next chapter,” thereby making the two into one chapter.].

### 148. Concerning the Parish of Another Presbytery

Let no presbyter presume to sing Mass in another presbyter’s parish [Col. 0532B], unless he is traveling; nor may he dare to receive a tithe belonging to another [Note: [Col. 0531] *alteram* (“another,” feminine), 5.].

### 149. Concerning the Boundaries of Churches

Let each church have a boundary specifying from which villages it is to receive tithes [Note: [Col. 0531] The words “from which villages it is to receive tithes” are absent in 5.].

### 150. Concerning the Property of Presbyters [Note: [Col. 0531] Located between *K. M. Langob.* chapter 137 in Muratori.]

Let each presbyter leave to the church the property which he acquires after the day of his consecration as his own [Note: [Col. 0531] *proprias* is superscribed or corrected to *propriae* (“of his own church”) in 1*; 2, 3, B., Bal. read “the property of his church.”] [Note: [Col. 0531] Vn. adds: “which the canons prohibit them from retaining.”].

### 151. Concerning Penitents Not to Be Compelled

Let no presbyter or layman invite a penitent to drink wine [Note: [Col. 0531] absent in Bal.] or eat meat unless he has, for him, given at the time, according to the degree of his penance, one [Note: [Col. 0531] *uno* (“one”), 2.] or two denarii [Note: [Col. 0531] C., Camb., Sang., Pal., Reg., Pith., Trec., and Bal. add “or three.”].

### 152. Concerning the Presbyters from Whom They Should Keep Away

Let no presbyter write charters [Note: [Col. 0531] *cartam* (“a charter”), V., Vn., M.; chapter 96 in K. and M., 3.], nor be the steward [Note: [Col. 0531] Vn. explains *conductor* as “that is, *masnerius*”; 3 reads *conditor* (“founder”).] of his lord [Note: [Col. 0531] “of his lords,” Langbd., G., Pal., Colb., Sangall.; “of his lord,” Norm.].

### 153. Concerning Where Burial Is Not to Take Place

Let no one henceforth bury a dead person in a church.

### 154. Concerning Preaching and the Chapters of Presbyters

Let each presbyter have chapters concerning greater and lesser vices [Note: [Col. 0531] *vicis* (“vices”), 1, 2; *viciis*, 2b, 5.] by which he may be able to recognize and preach to his subjects [Note: [Col. 0531] The words “preach … let them beware” are absent in 4.] that they should beware of the snares of the devil [Note: [Col. 0531] “service,” 2b, 4, 6.].

### 155. Concerning the Eucharist

Let the presbyter always have the Eucharist prepared [Note: [Col. 0531] absent in 5.], so that whenever someone becomes ill [Note: [Col. 0531] G.: “has become ill”; 2b: “when someone is ill or a sick child …”], or a small child is ill, he may immediately give him communion, lest he die without communion.

### 156. Concerning Having Two Cruets at the Lord’s Supper

Let the presbyter carry two cruets with him at the Lord’s Supper [Note: [Col. 0531] Three in G.; Vat., 1, Reg., Trec., Colb., and Sang. read “three”; 4 corrects *duos* (“two”) to “three”; Rem. and Bell. read “two or three”; 2b, second hand.], one for chrism and the other for oil with which to anoint catechumens or the sick [Note: [Col. 0533] 1, 1*, 2, 3, 5, 6, and Bal. have “or the sick”; a second hand in 2b adds *in* (“in”) between “or” and “the sick”; B. has a third cruet for anointing catechumens and another for oil for anointing the sick; G. has a third for the oil of the sick.], according to apostolic teaching. Whenever someone is ill, let him summon the presbyters of the church, and let them pray over him, anointing him with oil in the name of the Lord.

### 157. Concerning Ninths [Note: [Col. 0533] *annonis* (“of provisions”), G.] and Tithes

Let those who hold the benefices of churches give a ninth and a tenth from them to the church whose property it is [Note: [Col. 0533] “the whole tithe from them,” 3.]. And let those who hold such a benefice work it for a half-share [Note: [Col. 0533] “so that they work toward half,” 3, 4, B., Rem., N.; “and toward half,” Bal.; “wherefore,” Par.; “as far as,” Vat.; “whereby,” G.; “which,” Colb.], and [Note: [Col. 0533] omitted in 3 and G.; 5 and 6 (?) read *ut laborant* (“that they work”); Bal. *ut*; 1* “and to the same portion.”] from their portion let them give tithes to their own presbyter [Note: [Col. 0533] absent in 1*.].

### 158. Concerning the Feasts of the Year

These [Note: [Col. 0533] *haec* (“these,” neuter), 1*, 2, 3, 4, B.] are the feasts of the year which are to be honored in every respect:

The Nativity of the Lord; Saint Stephen; Saint John the Evangelist; the Holy Innocents; the octave of the Lord [Note: [Col. 0533] *octabes*, 3; “octave,” B.]; Epiphany [Note: [Col. 0533] absent in 3 and 6; “octave of Epiphany” absent in 1 and 2]; the octave of Epiphany; the Purification of Saint Mary; eight days of Easter; the greater litany [Note: [Col. 0533] *maiore* (“greater”), 5; *maiora* (“greater”), B.]; the Ascension of the Lord [Note: [Col. 0533] *assensio* (“ascension”), 3]; Pentecost; Saint John the Baptist; Saints Peter and Paul; Saint Martin; and Saint Andrew.

Concerning the Assumption of Saint Mary, we have left the matter to be inquired into [Note: [Col. 0533] Bal. reads *relinquimus* (“we leave”); compare Book II, chapter 33, where this feast is found to have been accepted by the authority of the Council of Mainz in 813.].

### 159. Concerning the Admonition of Priests

Let priests admonish the people to give alms and to pray for the various afflictions that we continually suffer because of our sins [Note: [Col. 0533] *assiduae* (“continual”), 5.].

### 160. Concerning Preaching to the People

Let each of the priests strive, according to his order, to preach and teach the people entrusted to him.

### 161. Concerning Drunkenness

Concerning drunkenness: first of all, let the elders themselves beware of it and show their juniors a good example of sobriety.

### 162. Concerning Admonition to Everyone

Everyone in general is to be admonished, in accordance with evangelical authority, so that their good works may shine before human beings [Note: [Col. 0533] absent in 3] and they may glorify God who is in heaven [Note: [Col. 0533] The words “who is in heaven” are absent in 4. After this, 1 adds a canon of Siricius, from which chapter 789, I. 51, is taken, but without an inscription and without being mentioned in the table of contents; it is separated from the preceding text by a larger space. 2b, 6, and Hld. likewise include it with the title “Concerning Conjugal Veiling.”].

## HERE BEGINS THE SHORT PREFACE TO THE SECOND BOOK [Note: [Col. 0533] 3: *i. prefatio l. s. salice legis* (abbreviated title variant).]

[Col. 0533]

[Col. 0533B] Above, in the first book [Note: [Col. 0533] “book,” B.; “booklet,” Bal.], I gathered together the ecclesiastical chapters which Lord Emperor Charles composed [Note: [Col. 0533] “which were gathered together,” B.]. In this book, however, I have written down those ecclesiastical matters which Lord Emperor Louis, the most devout Caesar [Col. 0534B], and Lothar, his son and emperor [Note: [Col. 0533] absent in 5.], published [Note: [Col. 0533] “the most devout published,” with the remainder absent, B., 6, Bal.; “the published matters were recorded,” B.].

[Col. 0533]
