## The aforesaid chapters and their text begin.

[Col. 0535]

[Col. 0535A] 1. Preface. We do not doubt that it is known to all of you either by sight or by hearing that our father [Note: [Col. 0535] “our fathers” in 3. and G.] and our forefathers, after they had been chosen by God for this purpose, devoted themselves especially to ensuring that the honor of the holy Church of God and the proper condition of the kingdom should endure. We too, following their example according to our measure, have often taken care to admonish your devotion concerning these matters, and by God’s mercy we now see many things amended and corrected [Note: [Col. 0535] “seized” corrected to “corrected” in 1*]. Therefore we ought both to render fitting praises to God and to offer manifold thanks for your good intention [Note: [Col. 0535] “we ought to offer” in 4; the initial *a* is erased in B.].

2. On divine providence in the constitution of the lord emperor, and on preserving the three chapters. But since it has pleased divine providence to appoint our mediocrity for the purpose of governing the care of his holy Church and of this kingdom [Note: [Col. 0535] “we should govern” in B.], we too desire to strive for this, together with our sons and associates, throughout the days of our lives: namely, that three matters in particular be preserved, with God’s help [Note: [Col. 0535] *in* is superscribed above *t* in 1*.], both by us and by you [Note: [Col. 0535] “both by us and by you” is absent in G.], in the administration of this kingdom; that is, that the defense, advancement, and fitting honor of the holy Church of God and of his servants should endure, and that peace and justice should be preserved throughout the entire community of our people. We desire above all to devote ourselves to these matters and to admonish you concerning them in all the assemblies that, with God’s help, we shall hold with you, as is our duty.

3. On the fact that the lord emperor is the admonisher of the faithful, and that all the faithful are his helpers [Note: [Col. 0535] Absent in 3. and B.]. Although the chief burden of this ministry appears to rest in our person, nevertheless it is recognized that, both by divine authority and by human arrangement, it has been divided among the several parts in such a way that each of you is understood to possess, in his own place and order, a share of our ministry. [Col. 0535D] Hence it is evident [Note: [Col. 0535] “it is evident” in 1*.] that I ought to be the admonisher of all of you [Note: [Col. 0535] “that I should be very much…” in 4. and 6.; “indeed” in Hludowicus], and that all of you ought to be our helpers. For we are not unaware of what is fitting for each of you in the portion entrusted to him [Note: [Col. 0535] “for each one” in 4. and B.; “in place of” in G.]. Therefore we cannot refrain from admonishing each one according to his own order [Note: [Col. 0535] “each one” in 1*.].

4. On the sacred ministry of bishops, and on the lord emperor’s admonition to the bishops. But since we know that it especially belongs to bishops to approach justly in the first place the reception of the sacred ministry, to live religiously in that ministry, to offer the peoples entrusted to them the way of life both by living well and by preaching rightly, to ensure that holy religion [Note: [Col. 0535] “rule” in 4.] is observed [Note: [Col. 0535] “is to be preserved” in 3.] in the monasteries established in their dioceses [Note: [Col. 0535] Absent in 6.] and that each person truly lives according to his profession, and to devote care to this [Note: [Col. 0535] “let him devote care” in 1., 3., and G.], we admonish and exhort all of you who have been established in this sacred order and who exercise pastoral office to strive especially in this matter [Note: [Col. 0535] “let us strive” in 3.], and, both by yourselves and through those subject to you, to be true helpers to us in the administration of the ministry entrusted to us, insofar as this pertains to your ministry [Note: [Col. 0535] “to you” in 3.; “the administration of the ministry” in 1. and 4.], so that at the judgment we may deserve not to be condemned for our negligence and yours, but rather to be rewarded for the good zeal of both. And wherever, through the negligence of an abbot, abbess, count, or vassal of ours [Note: [Col. 0535] “vessel” in B.], or of any other person [Note: [Col. 0535] “of anyone whatsoever” in 1*], you encounter some obstacle or difficulty in this matter, do not delay to make it known to us in due time. Thus, supported by our assistance, you may more easily accomplish, with our power serving as it ought, what your authority requires. [Col. 0536C] [Note: [Col. 0535] Between this chapter and the next B. left blank a space of more than one page.]

5. On the lord emperor’s admonition to bishops concerning the priests entrusted to their care, and concerning schools. Concerning the priests entrusted to your care, apply great diligence [Note: [Col. 0535] “apply diligence” in 1*.], so that you may teach and admonish them, with great care, how they ought to live and how they may benefit the peoples belonging to their charge, both by example and by word [Note: [Col. 0535] “teaching and admonition” in 3; “and admonish them” in 6. and G.; “and Bal.”], and so that they may be compelled by your pontifical authority to strive to do this. Whatever is justly reproved in them by the peoples, let your foresight not neglect to correct through the example of your own conduct [Note: [Col. 0535] Absent in 4.]. Moreover, lest the churches entrusted to them [Note: [Col. 0535] “the churches” in 1.] be neglected by them in restoration or in the provision of lights [Col. 0536D] according to their means, your diligence must nonetheless keep watch over this [Note: [Col. 0535] *nichilhominibus* (“nonetheless”) in 1*.]. And just as you forbid [Note: [Col. 0535] *prohibetis*, corrected from *prohibitis*, in 1*.] others to take anything from the estates assigned for the church lights [Note: [Col. 0535] “from those giving to the church lights” in 1*; “from the estates assigned for the church lights” in 3; “from the estates for the lights” in G.], so you and your archdeacons should provide an example to others by taking nothing from those same estates. Rather, let them be permitted to serve the purpose for which they were given, so that, as has been said, the whole may be applied, through your authority and zeal, to the restoration of churches and to the provision of lights. Schools, moreover, for instructing or teaching the sons and ministers of the Church, as you promised us previously at Attigny [Note: [Col. 0537] “Attigny” in 1* and 3; “at Attigny” in G.] and as we charged you, should not be neglected by you but established in suitable places wherever this has not yet been accomplished, for the benefit and advancement of many [Note: [Col. 0537] “should not be neglected” is plural in 1* and 3.].

6. On the admonition to counts for the benefit of the holy Church of God. To you counts we speak and admonish you, because it especially belongs to your ministry to show reverence [Note: [Col. 0537] *rem* (“a thing”) in 6.] and honor to the holy Church of God, to live in harmony with your bishops, to provide them assistance in carrying out their ministry, to establish peace and justice yourselves in your ministries, and to strive diligently to carry out in your ministries what our authority publicly decrees should be done [Note: [Col. 0537] “because things are decreed by the authority of the public ministry” in G.]. Therefore we admonish your faithfulness [Note: [Col. 0537] “your good fortune” in 3.] to remember the faith promised to us and, in the portion of our ministry entrusted to you [Note: [Col. 0537] “of your ministry” in 4.; “entrusted portions” in 1*.], namely, the making of peace and justice, to show yourselves before God and before human beings such that you may justly be called and regarded as our true helpers and as protectors of the people. Let no cause whatsoever, acceptance of gifts, friendship or hatred toward anyone, fear or favor compel you to deviate from the state of uprightness, so that you always judge justly between one neighbor and another. Be helpers and defenders of orphans, widows, and the other poor, and, according to your ability, honorers of the holy Church and of its servants [Note: [Col. 0537] “of the holy Church of God” in 1*. and G.]. Those who, through recklessness and violence, attempt to disturb the common peace of the people by theft and robbery [Col. 0537C] [Note: [Col. 0537] *latronia* (“robbery”) in 1*.] or plunder [Note: [Col. 0537] *latrociniis* (“robberies”) in B.] restrain through your zeal and correction, as is fitting [Note: [Col. 0537] “correct them” in 3.]. And if any person should hinder you in any way from being able to do what we command, let this be made known to us in due time, so that, assisted by our authority, you may worthily fulfill your ministry [Note: [Col. 0537] “our ministry” in G.].

7. On the admonition to laymen concerning the preservation of ecclesiastical honor. We admonish all laymen to preserve ecclesiastical honor, to show fitting reverence to bishops and the priests of God, to attend devoutly with their households when those priests preach, and reverently to observe the fasts jointly proclaimed by them, and to teach and compel their people to observe them. Let all strive also to honor and keep Sunday as is fitting. And [Note: [Col. 0537] Absent in 3.] so that this may be done more freely [Note: [Col. 0537] “may be done” plural in 3.], let markets and judicial assemblies be prohibited by the counts on that day, as has often been admonished.

8. On the admonition to abbots and laymen concerning monasteries entrusted to them through royal generosity. We also specially command abbots and laymen that, in the monasteries which they possess through our generosity [Note: [Col. 0537] Absent in 1.; “they possess” is placed after the following words in 3.], they should carry out, with the counsel and instruction of the bishops, whatever pertains to the religious life of canons, monks, and nuns [Col. 0538A], and should willingly hear and obey their salutary admonition in this matter.

9. On the admonition to bishops [Note: [Col. 0537] “monks” in G., both here and in the index.], abbots, and all the faithful concerning assistance to counts. We say again to bishops, abbots, our vassals, and all lay faithful that you should be helpers to the counts in administering justice [Note: [Col. 0537] In B. *omnibus* is present, but *ad iustitias faciendas* (“in administering justice”) is absent.].

10. On the admonition to bishops or counts concerning concord among themselves and with the other faithful. Let bishops and counts live harmoniously both with one another and with the other faithful, and let them mutually provide one another assistance in carrying out their ministries.

11. On the admonition to everyone generally, and concerning mutual charity and peace. We also say to everyone generally that you should have charity and peace toward one another [Note: [Col. 0537] “that we should have” in 3.], that you should be diligent to observe our general command generally, and that, out of regard for our honor, you should show honor to our envoys whom we have sent for whatever ecclesiastical or public benefit or need, and should not neglect to do what we command through them out of reverence for our authority [Note: [Col. 0537] Absent in 3.].

12. On the fact that each bishop or count should possess a share of the royal ministry, and on their testimony to one another. And since, as we have said, each of you is recognized as possessing a share of our ministry in its several parts [Note: [Col. 0537] “in its several parts” is absent in 1.], we wish to investigate, through public informers and every other reliable indication, and through our envoys whom we shall appoint for this purpose, how diligently each person has striven in this matter [Col. 0538C], and to discover through common testimony—namely, that of bishops concerning counts and of counts concerning bishops—how much the counts love and practice justice, how religiously the bishops conduct themselves and preach [Note: [Col. 0537] Absent in 3.], and, through the report of both groups, to learn about the fairness, peace, and concord of the other faithful engaged in their ministries [Note: [Col. 0537] “so that we may be able to learn” in 4.]. Likewise, we wish all of them, and they all, when questioned by us about their common association and condition, to be able to give one another true testimony.

13. On a matter arising that concerns the dishonoring of the kingdom. And if any such matter should arise in any province or county [Note: [Col. 0537] “some province” in 4.], one that concerns either the dishonoring of the kingdom or common harm [Note: [Col. 0537] Absent in 1* and 4.], and that cannot be corrected without our power, do not allow it to remain hidden from us for long, since we must correct everything with God’s help. For whatever has hitherto [Note: [Col. 0537] Absent in G.] been neglected, either by us or by you, in matters concerning the peace and justice of the whole people, and the honor of the kingdom [Note: [Col. 0537] “and concerning” in G. and Bal.], and the common good, we must strive, with God’s help, to ensure that from now on it is amended through our joint zeal [Note: [Col. 0537] “how it may be amended from now on through our zeal” in 1*, 4., 6., B., G., and Bal.].

14. On preserving peace during a military journey. Concerning the peace to be maintained during a military journey as far as the march [Note: [Col. 0539] “mark” in 1*.], we wish this to be made known to everyone: whoever knows by name the person responsible for damage inflicted upon him in the past year [Note: [Col. 0539] “knows” in 4.] should seek and receive justice from him.

15. On the announcement that those who go to war should each know his own men who are in his service [Note: [Col. 0539] In B.: “On the announcement that those who go to war”; the rest is absent.]. Henceforth, however, we wish to announce to everyone that each person should know all those who travel on such a journey in his service, whether they are his own men or others, so that he may know that he will have to give an account of their actions. Whatever they themselves do wrong in violating the peace must pertain to his *plevium* [Note: [Col. 0539] The readings are: *pleuium* in 1*; *pliuium* in 3., Bell., and Til.; *pluuium* in B., Pith., Par., and Div.; *pluvium*, corrected to *plivium*, in Rem.; *peculium* in N.; and *periculum* in the remaining witnesses. The precise reading is uncertain.]. The condition is, of course, that the violator of the peace first pay fitting penalties according to the nature of his crime, whether before us or before our envoy [Note: [Col. 0539] “before us or before our envoy” is absent in G.]. And the lord who has taken along with him a man whom he either was unwilling or unable to compel to observe our command and who was not afraid to commit plunder in our kingdom shall, for that man’s negligence—if he did not previously admonish him concerning these matters, and, after the negligence of the contemptuous man came to his knowledge, neglected to correct him as was fitting—be deprived of his honor. Thus neither of them shall remain without just vengeance [Note: [Col. 0539] “neither of them shall remain” plural in 3. Here 2 adds four chapters.].

16. On the dishonoring of the king through the negligence of those who receive embassies improperly. Concerning the dishonoring of the king and kingdom [Note: [Col. 0539] Absent in 3. and G.], and the evil reputation spread among foreign nations because of the negligence of those who either receive embassies sent to us improperly at their stations [Col. 0539C], or do not provide the prescribed provisions, or refuse to supply transport animals [Note: [Col. 0539] *parva reddare* in 1* [materially uncertain]; *parva redos* in 3.; and *parvareda* in G.], or secretly steal something from them [Note: [Col. 0539] “by stealth” in 1. and B.], or—what is most grievous—do not fear to inflict open violence upon them by beating them and plundering their property, we wish this to be known to everyone: whoever among those who hold our honors [Note: [Col. 0539] “holds” in 3.] does not henceforth strive to amend this negligence [Note: [Col. 0539] Absent in 1*. and 4.; 4., 6., B., and G. read variants meaning “does not strive … instruct … compel,” etc.], and does not instruct his men, who ought to perform this duty in his place, to carry it out properly, or does not compel them so that they dare not neglect it any longer [Note: [Col. 0539] “does not compel him” singular in 1.], and despises guarding the honor of ourselves and the kingdom entrusted to us [Note: [Col. 0539] “entrusted to you” in 3.], we do not wish him henceforth to possess either our honor or that of our kingdom [Note: [Col. 0539] “we wish” in 3., 6., and G.]. Rather, we wish each of our faithful to instruct his stewards of property specifically concerning these matters [Col. 0539D] [Note: [Col. 0539] “to instruct” plural in 4.], so that whenever and from wherever an embassy arrives, and they see either letters or an envoy, everyone may be able to receive it honorably in every place of our empire, for the sake of our honor and that of the entire kingdom [Note: [Col. 0539] “so that they do not neglect it” in G.].

17. On the places where embassies are to be received. [Col. 0540A] In those places where our father and we have now established by capitulary the road-service and lodging provisions [Note: [Col. 0539] “lodgings” in G.], let there be envoys specially appointed for this purpose to see continually to the matter, so that our faithful appointed for it may strive to prepare in due time everything necessary for receiving those embassies. Thus it will not then be necessary, when the time comes to provide or pay them, to seek out or bring things from far away. In all other places throughout our empire, let each of our faithful, both personally and through his ministers, exercise diligent vigilance, as we have said [Note: [Col. 0539] “let them exercise” plural in 3.].

18. On the admonition concerning one currency [Note: [Col. 0539] “admonish” in 1*.]. Concerning the currency, about which we have already issued admonitions for three years and established the time when one currency should be retained and all the others cease [Col. 0540B], we wish this to be made known to everyone: so that it may quickly be corrected without any excuse, we have decided to grant time until the feast of Saint Martin, so that each count may then have fulfilled our command concerning this matter in his ministry [Note: [Col. 0539] “by this command of ours” in 1.]. From that day onward, therefore, not another currency [Note: [Col. 0539] “any other” in B.], but that one alone, is to be used by everyone throughout our kingdom, in accordance with the constitution established in the chapters that we gave concerning this matter to those counts in whose ministries currency is struck. For at that time we wish to send our envoys through each county for this purpose, to investigate carefully how the counts have striven to fulfill our command concerning it [Note: [Col. 0539] “our command” in 1*. and B.]. And whoever is found negligent in this matter is to be ordered to come as quickly as possible into our presence [Col. 0540C] and give an account whether he was unwilling or unable to do what we commanded; or, if [Note: [Col. 0539] Absent in 1., 4., and G.] some obstacle prevented him from doing it [Note: [Col. 0539] “whether he was able, or …” in G.], why he did not report that impossibility to us in due time [Note: [Col. 0539] Absent in 1*.]. For if he was unwilling, or was unable because of his own negligence [Note: [Col. 0539] “if he or his subordinate…” in 3.], we wish to find someone who is willing and able to observe what we command. Moreover, so that our command in this matter may be fulfilled more quickly, whoever from that day onward brings out another denarius for the purpose of trading is to have it taken away from him by the count and his ministers.

19. On unjust tolls. Likewise, concerning unjust tolls—concerning which we have both established in chapters how they are to be observed by everyone and issued very frequent admonitions [Col. 0540D]—we wish our aforesaid envoys to conduct an investigation: by whom our command in this matter has been fulfilled and by whom it has been neglected. We wish the person who has neglected or delayed to fulfill it to be ordered to come into our presence, so that he may quickly give an account of these matters, as we said above. And if he is found guilty, let him receive fitting correction, so that he may provide an example of fear to the other negligent persons.

20. On renewing bridges where they formerly existed. Wherever bridges existed in ancient times, and in those places where, at the time of our father, they were built at his command for various necessities [Note: [Col. 0541] “have been built” in B. and Bal.; “existed” in G.], let them be restored and renewed without any delay by those who built them then [Note: [Col. 0541] “then them” in 1*.], so that they are restored by the feast of Saint Andrew—unless perhaps the size of the work itself or a flood of waters in any place [Note: [Col. 0541] “a flood in any place” in 1. and Bal.] prevents this. Otherwise, let no one presume, under any pretext, to neglect or delay the matter, but let it be completed by the aforesaid time. We wish our envoys, whom we mentioned above, to report in which places our command has been fulfilled, in which it has been neglected, and in which it has been delayed because of some impossibility or definite reason.

21. On the ninths [Note: [Col. 0541] “grain supplies” in G.] and tenths. Concerning the ninths [Note: [Col. 0541] “grain supplies” in G.] and tenths, about which both our father and we have often issued admonitions at various assemblies and have established through our capitularies how they are to be observed, we wish and command that from every crop, and from wine and hay [Note: [Col. 0541] “fodder” in 1*.], the ninth and tenth be faithfully and fully paid by everyone. As for *nutrimen* (“livestock increase”) as the tenth [Note: [Col. 0541] *nutrimento* (“nourishment”) in G. and in the superscript of 4.], let the custom observed until now be maintained by everyone. If, however, any bishop wishes to receive silver in place of this, the matter shall remain within his discretion, according to what is agreed between him and the person who must make the payment.

[Col. 0541C] 22. On works to be completed for the restoration of churches. Likewise, concerning works for the restoration of churches, whether in carrying them out or redeeming them, the will of the bishop should rather be followed [Note: [Col. 0541] “in restoration” in 4. and B.]. Nevertheless, it must in no way remain undone that, as we have often commanded, this or that payment be made to the churches’ portions. Let this also be known to everyone: whoever acts negligently in this matter and is found negligent in it before us, we wish him to undergo in full what we established in our capitulary concerning this matter with the common counsel of our faithful.

23. On counts, that they should be helpers to the ministers of the Church in their ministries. Let counts become helpers in every respect to the ministers of the Church in their ministries [Note: [Col. 0541] “and” in 1*. and B.; “in their ministry” is absent in 1. and 1*. and appears as “their ministry” in G.], so that they may be able to obtain this more fully both from our men, from themselves, and from their own people [Col. 0541D]. And whoever, after being admonished once and twice by the count concerning these matters, has not corrected himself [Col. 0542A], we wish his negligence to be reported to us by that same count, so that by our authority he may be compelled to undergo what is contained in our capitulary [Note: [Col. 0541] “contains” in 1*. and B.; “is absent” in 1.].

24. On the chapters to be received by archbishops and counts from the palace chancellor [Note: [Col. 0541] “from them, from the bishops” in 4.]. We also wish the chapters that have now been established by us, and those that may be established at another time with the counsel of our faithful, to be received from our chancellor by the archbishops and counts of their own cities, either personally or through their envoys. Each one is then to have them copied throughout his diocese for the other bishops, abbots, counts, and other faithful of ours [Note: [Col. 0541] “and other counties” is absent in 1*.], and have them read aloud in his counties before everyone [Note: [Col. 0541] “read them aloud before everyone” in 1.; “let them be reread” in 3. and G.], so that our ordinance and will may be made known to all. Our chancellor, however, is to note the names of the bishops and counts who take care to receive them [Note: [Col. 0541] “let them note” in 1*.], and report them to us, so that no one may presume to omit this. We also wish our vassals and under-vassals who serve us to receive fitting honor among everyone, as has often been admonished by our father and by us [Note: [Col. 0541] “has been admonished up to this point” in 6.].

25. On the names of the places in which the royal envoys carry out their embassy. At Besançon [Note: [Col. 0541] “Vesonicum” in G.], which is the diocese of Archbishop Bernoinus [Note: [Col. 0541] “Bernoni” in 1*, erased in G.; “Berneini” in 6.], Bishop Heiminus and Count Monogoldus [Note: [Col. 0541] “Manogoldus” in B.; “Monegoldus” in G.]. At Mainz [Note: [Col. 0541] “Magontia” in B. and G.; “Magontio” in 4.], which is the diocese of Archbishop Heistulfus, the same Heistulfus, bishop, and Ruodbertus, count [Note: [Col. 0541] The name appears as “Rotbertus” in 1*, 3., and G.; “Ruadpertus” in 6.; “Ruatpertus” in 4.; “Hruotbertus” in B.]. At Trier, Archbishop Hetti [Note: [Col. 0541] “Hettus” in 1*; “Hetdi” in 1.; “Hecti” in 3.; “Haecti” in G.] and Count Adalbertus. At Cologne, Archbishop Hadaboldus [Note: [Col. 0541] “Hadabaldus” in 1*; “Hadalpoldus” in 4. and 6.] and Count Eemundus [Note: [Col. 0541] “Heemunt” in G.]. At Reims, Archbishop Ebo [Note: [Col. 0541] “Ebbo” in G. and Bal.; “Eddo” in 3.], whenever he can; and when he cannot, Bishop Ruothadus [Note: [Col. 0541] “Hruotadus” in 1* and B.; “Hruatchadus” in 4. and 6.; “Hrothardus” in 3.; “Hruotchardus” in G.] in his place, together with Count Hruotfridus [Note: [Col. 0541] “Hruatfridus” in 6.], over six counties, namely Reims, Châlons [Note: [Col. 0541] The name appears as “Catolon” in 1.; “Catholon” in 1*; “Catalon” in 3., B., and G.], Soissons [Note: [Col. 0541] Various forms include “Suasion,” “Suasonis,” “Suason,” “Suasonon,” and “Suasionon.”], Senlis, Beauvais, and Laon. Over the four bishoprics that belong to the same diocese—namely Noyon, Amiens, Thérouanne [Note: [Col. 0541] “Tarvianensem” in 3.; “Tarvanassem” in B.], and Cambrai [Note: [Col. 0541] “and Cambrai” is absent in G.]—Bishop Ragnarius [Note: [Col. 0541] The name appears as “Rangarius,” “Ragengarius,” “Sangarius,” “Regenarius,” and other forms in the cited witnesses.] and Count Berengarius. At Sens, Archbishop Hieremias and Count Donatus [Note: [Col. 0541] B. reads “Natus”; 4., Herold, Rivipull, Thuan, Palat, Sang, and Colb. read “Donatus and Ingobertus, counts.”] [Note: [Col. 0541] “Count” and the following initials are absent in 1. and 4.]. At Rouen [Note: [Col. 0541] “Rotumacum” in 1* and B.; “Ruothomacum” in G.], Archbishop Willibertus [Note: [Col. 0541] “Willebertus” in 3.; “Wilgebertus” in B.] and Count Ingobertus [Note: [Col. 0541] “Sigobertus” in 1*.]. At Tours, Archbishop Landramnus and Count Hruodbertus [Note: [Col. 0541] “Rhuobertus” in 1*; “Rotbertus” in 3. and G.]. At Lyon, Tarentaise, and Vienne, Bishop Albericus [Note: [Col. 0541] “count” in 1.] and Count Rihhardus [Note: [Col. 0541] “Richardus” in 1*, 3., and B.; “Ribchardus” in 4.].

26. On the memorandum concerning the embassy of the aforesaid envoys. A memorandum of what pertains to the embassy of the aforesaid envoys. First, they are to assemble an assembly in two or three places [Note: [Col. 0543] “at an assembly” in 6.], where all those concerned with their embassy [Note: [Col. 0543] “their embassy” in the reversed order *eorum ad* in 1.] can gather. They are to make known generally to everyone what their embassy is: namely, that they have been appointed and sent by us [Note: [Col. 0543] “by God” in G.] for this purpose, so that if any bishop or count [Note: [Col. 0543] “any” in the form *quislibet* in 1*.] is unable, because of some impediment [Note: [Col. 0543] *ad* through *non possit* is absent in G.], to fulfill his ministry, he may have recourse to them and, with their assistance [Note: [Col. 0543] “admonition” in 1*.], fulfill his ministry [Note: [Col. 0543] “his ministry through whatever assistance” in 1*.]. If there is a matter that cannot be corrected through their admonition [Note: [Col. 0543] “correct” in 1*.], it is to be brought through them to our attention. And if a bishop or count has acted somewhat negligently in his ministry [Note: [Col. 0543] “they have acted” in 4.], he is to be corrected through the admonition of these men. Let all the people know that they have been appointed for this purpose [Note: [Col. 0543] Absent in 1*.]: whoever, through the negligence [Note: [Col. 0543] “through admonition or injury” in 4.], carelessness, or inability of a count [Note: [Col. 0543] “of counts” in 1*.], has been unable to obtain his justice, may first bring his complaint to them and obtain justice through their assistance. And whenever anyone has appealed to us in a matter of necessity [Note: [Col. 0543] “has retreated” in 6.], we may refer the complaints reported to us to them for settlement. The envoys themselves, however, are not to travel here and there without the clearest cause or necessity—unless they learn that something has arisen in anyone’s ministry, belonging to their embassy [Note: [Col. 0543] *pertinentem* in 3., B., and G.], that requires their presence and cannot be corrected without their counsel or assistance [Note: [Col. 0543] “their assistance” in 1*. and B.]. Nevertheless, they must be concerned [Note: [Col. 0543] Absent in 1*.] that nothing in their embassy remain uncorrected through their negligence [Col. 0543C]; but whenever they recognize a definite and genuine necessity, they must not neglect to fulfill our command.

27. On the fact that the matters enacted through the chapters should be made known to everyone by the royal envoys. We also wish it to be known to everyone that they have been appointed for this purpose: that whatever we establish generally through our chapters concerning any matters may be made known to all through them [Note: [Col. 0543] “through the envoys” in Bal.], and that the execution of these matters should depend upon their administration [Note: [Col. 0543] “should depend” singular in 4. and G.], so that they may be fulfilled by everyone. If, however, because of some such impediment as cannot be corrected by them [Note: [Col. 0543] Absent in 4. and 6.], anything that we have established and commanded should remain incomplete [Note: [Col. 0543] “whatever” in 1*.], let this be reported to us in due time by their account, so that what could not be corrected by them may be corrected by us [Col. 0543D] [Note: [Col. 0543] “what could not be corrected” in 1. and 4.; “what will not be able to be corrected” in G.].

## 28. On admonishing those who exercise a commission

We believe that you know how weighty is the commission that we have entrusted to you, and how dangerous it is to neglect responsibility for so great a matter—the responsibility which [Note: In 1*, *nos*, “we/us,” was corrected to *vos*, “you.”], as you do not fail to know, you have undertaken from [Note: *ex*, “from,” is absent in 1*.] our obligation for the common salvation of us all. [Note: Col. 0543: *p.* “before God” is added in the margin, 1.] Concerning this [Note: Witnesses 6 and B insert *re*, “matter.”], when we questioned you, [Col. 0544A] the answer given to us was not such that it could have sufficed for the same arrangement which the necessity of matters pertaining to the common good seemed to demand, or which could have afforded us some consolation of security. [Note: Col. 0543: *eam* “that” for *eandem*, 1*. and 3.; Baluze: the words “up to *potuisset*” are absent in G.] [Note: Col. 0543: *suppetere* “to be available,” 4; *parcere* “to spare,” 6; *parere* “to obey,” B.]

We perceived that this happened because, last year, when we gave you the capitulary concerning your commission, we ordered you to exercise careful vigilance, and that no injury should be inflicted without cause upon those whom we wish to be honored. [Note: Col. 0543: *item* “likewise,” 1*.] Therefore we wish to make known to you how, now with God’s help, you must fulfill this command of ours. [Note: Col. 0543: *domino* “the Lord,” 3, B.]

We wish our envoys—whom we have appointed for this purpose, namely, to take care and concern [Note: Manuscript 1 has the abbreviated reading *q. ut u.*, left unresolved by the edition.] that each person [Note: *qui*, “who,” is absent in 1*.] whom we have appointed as ruler of our people [Note: *est*, “is,” is absent in 1*.] administer the office entrusted to him in his own sphere justly and in a manner pleasing to God, for our honor and the benefit of our people—to make diligent inquiry in the following manner: whether the provisions contained in our capitulary, which we gave them last year, [Note: Col. 0543: *continentur*, “are contained,” is absent in 4.] have been fulfilled [Note: Col. 0543: *secundum*, “according to,” is absent in 4.] according to God’s will and our command.

Accordingly, we wish these same envoys, in the middle of May, to meet within each of their respective commissions with all the bishops, abbots, counts, and our vassals [Note: *vasis* for *vassis*, “vassals,” in 3 and B.], our advocates [Note: Col. 0543: *advocatis nostris*, “our advocates,” is absent in 3.], and the *vicedomini* of the abbesses, as well as with those who cannot come in person because of some unavoidable necessity, at one place. If circumstances require it for the convenience of assembling, let the same meeting be held in two or three places, especially for the sake of the poor of the people [Note: Col. 0543: *pauperes*, “the poor,” is absent in 4.], so that it may suit everyone [Note: Manuscript 3 reads *in omn.*, an abbreviated form of *in omnibus*, “for all.”]. [Col. 0544C]

Each count is also to bring with him his vicars and centenaries, and three or four of his leading *scabini*. [Note: Col. 0543: *scabiniis* in 1* and G; *scabineis* in 3, B, and Baluze.] At this meeting, first [Note: Manuscript 3 reads *proximum*, “next,” for *primum*, “first.”] let there be discussion of the Christian religion and ecclesiastical order; then let our envoys inquire from everyone how each of those whom we have appointed for this purpose administers in the people the office entrusted to him according to God’s will and our command, or [Note: Col. 0543: *ut cum*, B, G, Baluze.] how united and harmonious they are in this matter, and how they mutually assist one another in carrying out their duties. [Note: Col. 0543: *unames* “united,” 1*.]

They are to conduct this investigation so carefully and diligently that we may be able through them to learn the complete truth of the matter. If any such case is brought to their attention [Col. 0544D] as requires their assistance, then, according to the character of the cases contained in our capitulary, we wish them to go there and endeavor, by our authority, to correct what needs correction.

## 29. On not alienating property belonging to a venerable institution

No church established under Roman authority [Note: Col. 0543: *diccione* “jurisdiction,” 5.], nor any hospice for strangers [Note: Col. 0543: *xenodochium* is the form established in 3.], institution for the poor, hospital [Note: In 1*, the words from the second *vel* through *nosochomium* are omitted here and inserted below after *loco venerabili*; *vel nosochomium* is absent in B.], [Col. 0545A] orphanage, home for the aged, foundling home, or monastery of monks or holy women [Note: Manuscript 2 reads *que scae monialium*, “and of holy women.”] that has an abbot [Note: Col. 0545: *habent* “they have,” 1; another hand corrects it to *quae habeant* “which may have.”] or abbess [Note: Col. 0545: *archimanditrismam*, 1*; *archimandritissimam*, 5. Baluze inserts after this: “let no one presume to act contrary to these provisions.”] may alienate any immovable property: whether a house, a field, a garden, a rural slave, or civic bread. [Note: Col. 0545D: Such bread was customarily distributed by the Byzantine emperor.] Nor may it bind such property to creditors by way of a special mortgage [Note: Witness 4 has the abbreviated reading *n. a. cred. species*; G reads *creditores*, “creditors.”]. [Note: Col. 0545: *apothecae* “of a storage-house,” G.] [Note: Col. 0545: “nor to creditors” is absent in 4; G has “creditors.”]

The word “alienation” includes sale, gift, exchange, and a perpetual emphyteutic contract. [Note: Col. 0545: *amphiteoseos*, with the preceding words “that is,” in 2b; *et p.* “and a” in G.] All priests without exception [Note: Col. 0545: *ab huiusmodi* “from such,” 1* and 4, G, Baluze.] must therefore refrain from such alienation, fearing the penalties [Note: Manuscript 5 reads *panes*, “loaves,” for *poenas*, “penalties.”] threatened by the Leonine constitution: namely, that the purchaser must restore the property to the venerable institution to which it had previously belonged, together with the fruits and other profits [Note: Col. 0545: *aliisquae*, 2.] produced in the meantime; [Col. 0545B] and that the church’s steward [Note: *ecconomium* in 2b and 3; *echonomum* in G, for *hyconomum*, “steward.”] must repay all the profit that he has gained [Note: *sumpserit*, “has taken,” in 6, for *senserit*, “has gained/experienced.”] from such a prohibited alienation [Note: *quod ex se* is absent in 1*, 3, B, G, and Baluze; 2b has *q. si se h.* (“which, if he has taken it”); a second hand in 4 has *q. si ex se* (“which, if from it”).] or by which he has caused loss to the church [Note: Witness 6 and Baluze have *ecclesiae damnum*, “the church’s loss”; Baluze also has *vel qui ecclesiae damnum ... a ministerio submoveat*, “or whoever causes damage to the church is to be removed from office.”], and must thereafter cease to be its steward.

Not only he himself, but also his successors, are to be liable [Note: Baluze has the abbreviated *hac lege t.*, “are bound by this law.”], whether the chief steward himself made the alienation or, seeing a bishop alienating property, failed to prohibit him [Note: Col. 0545: *respias*, 1*; *respicies*, 3.]—still more if he consented. [Note: Manuscript 3 has the corrupt *si phibuerit m. m. sicul sens.*, which appears to mean “if he did not prohibit him.”]

The notary who drew up such prohibited instruments [Note: Col. 0545: *instrumenta* “instruments,” only Met. and Riv.] must be handed over to perpetual exile.

The magistrates who [Note: Manuscripts 1, 1*, and B read *et ad*, “and to,” at this point.] admitted these instruments [Note: Col. 0545: *qui in eadem* “who in the same [matter],” 3.], and the officials who assisted [Note: *ut*, “that,” is absent in 1, 1*, 2, 2b, 4, 6, B, and G.] [Note: The following *et*, “and,” is absent in 3 and G.] in having donations entered in the records [Note: Col. 0545: *int. et don.* “entered and donations,” G.] or other [Note: G reads *certe*, “certainly,” for *ceterae*, “other.”] alienations confirmed through the intervention of legal acts [Note: Col. 0545: G has *infirmentur*, “are invalidated,” instead of *confirmentur*, “are confirmed,”] must relinquish not only their magistracies [Note: Col. 0545: *magistratus*, 1, 1*, 2, 2b, 3, 4, B, G.] but also their rank and possessions. [Note: G has *dignitates aliae facult.*, “their other dignities and resources.”]

The constitution remits what was done in earlier times, but excepts [Note: *excipit*, “excepts,” in 3, 6, and G, for *excepit*.] certain contracts [Note: Col. 0545: *contractos*, 2, 2b, 5, B; *contra hoc*, 3.], which it explains in the following chapters [Note: Col. 0545: absent in 4 and 6.], by which the immovable property of churches may be alienated. [Note: Col. 0545: absent in 1* and 3.]

A hospice for strangers (*exenodochium*) is a venerable place in which travelers are received. An institution for the poor (*ptochotrophium*) is a venerable place in which poor and sick people are fed. [Note: Col. 0545: *pascantur* “may be fed,” 2.] A hospital (*nosochomium*) is a venerable place in which sick people are cared for. [Col. 0546A] [Note: Col. 0545: B has *pascuntur*, “are fed.”] An orphanage (*orphanotrophium*) is a venerable place in which children deprived of their parents are fed. [Note: Col. 0545: *gerontomium*, 4.] A home for the aged (*gerontochomium*) is a venerable place in which poor people weakened solely by old age are cared for. [Note: Col. 0545: *geronthomium*, 2, 2b, 5.] A foundling home (*brephotrophium*) is a venerable place in which infants are nourished.

## 30. On how property belonging to a holy institution may be transferred to the emperor

[Note: The supplied heading reads *quomodo liceat aa imperatorem res sancti loci transferre*; *aa* is apparently corrupt for *ad*, “to,” but the corruption is retained here.]

If the ruler wishes to grant an immovable property to a holy institution and receive another immovable property from it, thereby contracting an exchange, he may do so under a divine pragmatic sanction promulgated by him. [Note: Col. 0545: *pragmaticaque*, G.]

## 31. On assisting orphans and the disinherited

For the preservation of this concord of peace [Note: In 1*, *iustius* was corrected to *iustam*; the reading is attached to the otherwise printed *istius*.] [Note: Col. 0545: here begins the law among the Lombard manuscripts K, M, and Langobardic copies in V, Vn, E, and Muratori, p. 149.], we have therefore decided concerning orphans [Note: V, Vn, and E have the abbreviated *o. et pupillis et*, “orphans and wards and poor.”] and poor people who are said—whether rightly or wrongly—to have lost the inheritance belonging by law [Note: Col. 0545: *legibus*, “by law,” is absent in 1.] to them from their father or mother: if such persons are found anywhere whose fathers [Note: *patres*, “fathers,” is absent in 4.] or mothers [Note: *matres*, “mothers,” is absent in 4.] have disinherited them because of their conveyances (*traditiones*) [Note: Col. 0545: *traditionem*, “conveyance,” 2b.], through the persuasion or requests of others, or by some other device, we entirely wish and decree [Note: Col. 0545: *discernimus*, “we determine,” 3.] that the matter be remedied, insofar as it concerns us or our authority, according to the will of God and your holy admonition and consideration. [Note: Manuscript 3 has *nostram*, “our,” instead of *vestram*, “your.” G reads: *omnino volumus ad quem pertinet potestatem iuxta voluntatem domini et vestram decrevimus emendari, quantum ad nos vel ad nostram sanctam admonitionem* (“we entirely wish that it be remedied by whoever has authority, according to the will of the Lord and your holy admonition, insofar as it concerns us or our holy admonition”).]

Thus, if anything of this kind is found outside our official jurisdiction, we may dare to admonish your Clemency that it be corrected.

## 32. On not purchasing the property of poor or less powerful people under a wrongful pretext

[Note: Manuscripts 2 and 2b read *emendandis*, “to be corrected,” for *emendis*, “to be bought,” in the heading.]

For the protection of the poor, for whom we must take care, we have decided that neither bishops, abbots, counts, vicars, judges, nor anyone else at all may, under a wrongful pretext or by an evil device, dare either to purchase the property of poor or less powerful people or to take it from them by force. Whoever among them wishes to purchase something is to do so in a public court, before suitable witnesses, and with proper justification.

Wherever the contrary is found to have occurred, the transaction is to be completely corrected by our command. [Note: Col. 0545: *vestram* “your,” 2, 2b, 3, 6, G, Hild.]

[Col. 0545D]

The following two chapters are added by B, Pith., Paris., Norm., and by a second hand on an attached slip in the Rheims manuscript. Baluze inserted them into the text:

### 33. How justice is to be done to the poor

Concerning the cases of widows, wards, orphans, and other poor people: at the first meeting, before midday, their cases or complaints are to be heard and decided; after midday, the cases of the king, the churches, and powerful men are to be heard. For these poor people have no means by which they can support [Col. 0546D] [Pith., Paris., Norm.: “raise up”] themselves until justice is obtained for them, and for this reason they raise so many cries in our ears.

### 34. On people who bring unjust complaints

Concerning people who unjustly bring complaints against others: if someone is found who has no lawful basis for bringing or pursuing a claim, and is defeated in the case, he is to render justice according to law and equity for the false accusation he has made.

[Col. 0547A]

## 33. On the festivals of the year

We have decreed that the following holy days be celebrated during the year: Easter Sunday is to be honored with all reverence and sobriety; likewise, we have decreed that the entire following week be observed. The day of the Lord’s Ascension is to be celebrated fully. [Note: Col. 0547: absent in 2.] Pentecost is to be observed in the same way as Easter. One day is to be kept for the feast of the apostles Peter and Paul; the Nativity of Saint John the Baptist; the Assumption of Saint Mary [Note: Manuscript 3 has the abbreviated *M. et nativitatem ipsius d.*, “of Mary and her Nativity.”]; the dedication of Saint Michael; the feast [Note: *natalis* in 1 and *natale* in 3 and B, for *natalem*, “feast.”] of Saint Remigius [Note: Col. 0547: *Remei*, 1, 2; *Remedii*, 4.]; Saint Martin; Saint Andrew; four days for the Nativity of the Lord [Note: Col. 0547: *natalem*, 1*; absent in 2 and B.]; the octave of the Lord; the Epiphany of the Lord [Note: Col. 0547: *epiphania*, 2.]; and the Purification of Saint Mary.

We have also decreed that the festivals of those martyrs and confessors whose holy bodies rest in each parish be observed.

[Col. 0547B]

## 34. On ancient churches, so that they may retain their honor

Churches established in ancient times are not to be deprived either of tithes or of other possessions, so that these may be granted to new oratories. [Note: Col. 0547: the words “so that they may have their honor” are omitted here and placed after “anciently” in 3; 1 has *oratoribus*, “to orators.”]

## 35. On spiritual godchildren

We have further commanded that each godfather or spiritual relative instruct his spiritual children in the Catholic faith. [Note: Col. 0547: *spirituales*, B.]

## 36. On priests being irreproachable

[Note: This chapter is absent in 3 and 3b, although it appears in their index.]

In accordance with the Apostle’s saying, priests are to be irreproachable, adorned with good character, and in no way devoted to shameful profits, according to what Scripture says: “No one serving as a soldier for God entangles himself in secular affairs, so that he may please the one to whom he has proved himself.”

They must not only themselves abstain from shameful profits and usury, but must also instruct the peoples subject to them to abstain [Note: *abstinere*, “to abstain,” is absent in 4.] from these things.

[Col. 0547C]

## 37. On not accepting pledges from incestuous persons, from those who do not pay tithes, or from priests living negligently

We have been told that in certain places bishops and counts accept pledges from incestuous persons and from those who do not pay tithes, and from [Note: *a*, “from,” is absent in 2.] priests on account of certain negligences, and divide the money [Note: *pecuniam*, “money,” is absent in 6.] among themselves. We have decreed that this must be entirely abolished, lest an opportunity be given to avarice; and we have established that incestuous persons are to be punished with penance according to canonical judgment. Those who, after repeated admonitions and preaching by priests, neglect to pay tithes [Note: Col. 0547: *creberrimas*, “very frequent,” B and Baluze.] are to be excommunicated. We do not wish them to be bound by an oath [Note: B reads *volumus*, “we wish,” for *nolumus*, “we do not wish.”], because of the danger of perjury.

## 38. On discernment in receiving the Lord’s body and blood

Great discernment must be exercised in receiving the Lord’s body and blood. Care must be taken that, if reception is postponed for too long, this may become harmful to the soul, since the Lord says: “Unless you eat the flesh of the Son of Man and drink his blood, you will not have life in yourselves.”

But if it is received without discernment [Note: Col. 0547: *accipitur*, “is received,” 2b.], one must fear what the Apostle says: [Col. 0548A] “Whoever eats and drinks unworthily eats and drinks judgment upon himself.”

Therefore, according to the teaching of the same Apostle, a person must examine himself [Note: Witness 6 has the abbreviated *probet se h.*, “let the person prove himself.”] and then eat of that bread and drink from the cup. He should abstain for several days [Note: Col. 0547: absent in 6.] from works of the flesh and purify body and soul, preparing himself to receive so great a sacrament. This is in the example of David, who would never have received the bread of the Presence from the priest unless he had confessed that he had abstained from marital relations since yesterday and the day before yesterday.

## 39. On people of different conditions and those placed over them

Since it is evident that there are people of different conditions in the Church—noble and ignoble, slaves, tenant farmers, resident dependents, and others of this kind [Note: Col. 0547: *ceteri*, “the others,” 1, 2, 3, G.]—it is necessary that all clerics or laymen placed over them act toward them mercifully and treat them compassionately, whether in requiring labor from them or in receiving taxes and certain debts. [Col. 0548B] [Note: Col. 0547: *nomina*, “names,” absent in G; *omnia*, “all,” 4 and Baluze.]

They must know that these people are their brothers and that they have, together with them [Note: G reads *se*, “themselves,” for *secum*, “with them.”], one Father, God, to whom [Note: Manuscripts 2, 3, and G read *qui*, “who,” for *cui*, “to whom.”] they cry: “Our Father, who are in heaven”; and one mother, the holy Church, which gives them birth from the undefiled womb of the sacred font.

Therefore, discipline of the greatest mercy and suitable governance must be applied to them: discipline, so that by living without discipline they do not offend their Creator; governance, so that, deprived of the assistance of their superiors in the daily necessities of life [Note: Col. 0547: 4 has *necessitatibus*, “necessities,” instead of *commeatibus*, “daily provisions.”] they do not grow faint. [Note: Col. 0547: *fatescant*, corrected to *fatiscant*, “grow faint,” 1*.]

## 40. On what women and abbesses should be placed over women’s monasteries

Women and abbesses who know how to guard both themselves and the flock entrusted to them with great religious devotion and holiness should be placed over women’s monasteries and entrusted with them. [Col. 0548C] [Note: Col. 0547: G has *voluerint*, “may have wished,” instead of *noverint*, “may have known.”] They must not cease to benefit those over whom they preside, but must so watch over themselves and over them that they may be regarded as holy vessels prepared for the Lord’s service.

She must present herself to her subjects in such a manner—in her bearing, clothing, and entire way of life [Note: Col. 0547: *communi*, “common,” 1]—that she may provide them with guidance as they proceed toward the heavenly kingdom. [Note: B and Baluze read the plural forms *praebeant ... sciant ... acceperunt ... reddituras*, “they should provide ... they should know ... they have received ... they will render.”]

She must also know that, for those whom she has received under her governance, she will render an account before the sight of the Lord.

## 41. On incestuous persons and murderers who refuse to heed the admonitions of priests

Incestuous persons, parricides [Note: Col. 0547: *patricide*, “patricides,” 4.], and murderers [Note: Col. 0547: absent in 3.] are, alas, found among us in great numbers. Some of them refuse to heed the admonitions of priests, wishing [Col. 0548D] to persist in their former crimes. Those who refuse to be recalled from so wicked a habit by the saving warnings of priests must be restrained from it through the discipline of secular power.

We have already excommunicated some of them, but, making light of this [Note: Col. 0547: absent in 1*.], they have persisted in the same crimes. Therefore let your Mildness decide [Col. 0549A] what is to be done with such people from now on. [Note: Col. 0549: *est*, “is,” 1*, 2, 3, B.]

## 42. On admonishing lords concerning their subjects

The lords of subjects are to be admonished to act toward their own people piously and mercifully; not to condemn them on any unjust pretext; not to oppress them by force; not to take away their small possessions unjustly; and not to exact impiously or cruelly the very debts that are owed to the subjects. [Note: Col. 0549: *a subditis*, “from the subjects,” 3, 4, B, Baluze; *exigant*, “let them exact,” 3.]

## 43. On the communion of laypeople in the Lord’s body and blood

[Note: Manuscript 4 reads *communione*, “communion,” for *communicatione*, “participation,” in the heading.]

Laypeople are to receive communion, if not more frequently, at least three times a year, unless someone is prevented by some particularly serious crime.

## 44. On parents and godfathers educating children

Parents are to make every effort to educate their children, and godfathers those whom they receive from [Note: *de*, “from,” is absent in 3.] the font of baptism [Note: Col. 0549: G has *patribus*, “fathers,”]: parents, because they have begotten them and they have been given to them by the Lord; godfathers, because they stand as guarantors for them. [Note: Col. 0549: *perstudeant*, “strive earnestly,” 2, 2b, 6.]

## 45. On churches established in ancient times

Churches established in ancient times are to be deprived neither of tithes nor of any other possession. [Note: Col. 0549: *ab*, “from,” 4.]

## 46. On burial

Concerning the burial of the dead in basilicas, the constitution established by the ancient Fathers is to be observed. [Col. 0549A] [Note: In the Council of Nantes, canon 6; Baluze.]

# The third little preface of the book begins

[Col. 0549]

[Col. 0549B] In the two preceding books [Note: B and G read the abbreviated *d. libellis*, “two books.”] [Note: Manuscript 1* reads *capitularibus*, “capitularies,” for *capitula*, “chapters.”] I set out the ecclesiastical capitularies of the aforesaid princes, the lord Emperor Charles, and the lord and most glorious Augustus Louis, and the Caesar Lothar. [Note: Col. 0549: *nec non et*, “and also,” 1* and 5; *nec non*, 3; the words are absent in B, G, and Baluze.] Now, in this third little book, I have gathered together those provisions relating to the enlargement of secular law which the lord Emperor Charles issued. [Note: B reads *edidit, adnotata sunt in hoc tertio libro*, “which the lord Emperor Charles issued; they are recorded in this third book.”]

# The chapters begin

[Note: Manuscript 3 reads *I. C. SALICE LEGIS L. III.*, an abbreviated title: “Here begin the chapters of Book III of the Salic Law.”]

[Col. 0549]

[Col. 0549B]

1. On maintaining the peace.  
2. On general justice.  
3. On royal justice. [Note: Col. 0549D: absent in B, though not in the text.]  
4. On not carrying weapons.  
5. On the equipment to be taken to the army.  
6. On how far merchants may proceed.  
7. On complainers or advocates.  
8. On oaths.  
9. On conspiracies.  
10. On perjuries. [Col. 0549C]  
11. On advocates, *vicedomini*, vicars, and centenaries.  
12. On tolls.  
13. On counterfeit coins.  
14. On the *haribannum*.  
15. On the royal census.  
16. On free men who have fiscal wives.  
17. On the care of the royal envoys.  
18. On the equality to be established by the royal envoys.  
19. On those who hold royal benefices.  
20. On those who commit fraud concerning royal benefices.  
21. On those who are driven away in order to delay their own judicial case. [Note: The heading prints the passive *fugantur*, “are driven away”; the precise legal sense of *propriam iustitiam dilatandam* is uncertain.]  
22. On not carrying weapons to court.  
23. On thieves.  
24. On animals or other things, from whom they are to be bought. [Note: The heading prints *De animalibus vel aliis rebus, a quibus emantur*; the antecedent and syntax of *a quibus* are uncertain.]  
25. On the killings of clerics.  
26. On immunity, if some damage has been done there.  
27. On one who dares to assist another unjustly disputing against someone in court.  
28. On a man who has obtained freedom by charter.  
29. On a free man who gives himself over as a pledge.  
30. On royal debts and how they are to be paid. [Col. 0549D]  
31. On one who presumes to reopen a decided case.  
32. On what kind of person one summoned as a witness must be.  
33. On *scabini*, advocates, and notaries to be chosen by the royal envoys.  
34. On those who disdain to observe the law.  
35. On the *coniectum* of the *haribannator*. [Note: The heading prints *De haribannatoris coniecto*; the technical term *coniectum* is uncertain.]  
36. On tenant farmers and fiscal persons. [Col. 0550B]  
37. On not sending a man to court without cause.  
38. On the case of a drunken man, his testimony, and the count’s court.  
39. On royal envoys and other traveling officials.  
40. On those who are to be summoned to court.  
41. On false witnesses.  
42. On not swearing by the king’s life.  
43. On one who is free by charter, if he is summoned to service. [Col. 0550C]  
44. On a slave who commits any damage.  
45. On summoning according to law to the assembly.  
46. On the warrantor of a thing.  
47. On men condemned to death and later granted life, if they seek justice.  
48. On a man granted life after judgment, if he refuses to render justice.  
49. On a thief under the ban received by a free man.  
50. On a count who places a thief under the ban.  
51. On free men who must be compelled to come to the assembly.  
52. On witnesses summoned to give testimony and how they are to be brought forward.  
53. On no one delaying anyone’s justice.  
54. On not compelling anyone to go to a bridge for the sake of a toll.  
55. On whether a priest has given holy chrism to overturn a judgment.  
56. On what judges, advocates, officials, and other ministers should be like.  
57. On the public assembly.  
58. On oaths *adramitis* at the palace. [Note: The heading prints the corrupt or technical form *De sacramentis ad palatium adramitis*; its precise sense is uncertain.]  
59. On interference with complainers. [Col. 0550D]  
60. On fugitives concealed against the lord’s command.  
61. On excessively blasphemous thieves.  
62. On peace within the country.  
63. On restraining young men among the common people.  
64. On one who comes against a royal envoy with a crowd and weapons. [Note: Col. 0550D: *cum*, “with,” is absent in 1.]  
65. On one who breaks into another person’s house. [Col. 0551A]  
66. On crops or grain seized or stolen in the army.  
67. On a free man summoned to the army.  
68. On exacting the *haribannum*.  
69. On those who hold royal honors and, summoned to the army, do not come to the appointed assembly.  
70. On those who return from the army without permission.  
71. On those who hold the princes’ benefices.  
72. On not compelling anyone to drink in the army.  
73. On vassals still serving at the palace who nevertheless hold benefices.  
74. On preparations for the army according to ancient custom.  
75. On not giving or selling a coat of mail or sword to an outsider without royal permission.  
76. On the limits of cases and lawsuits.  
77. On bishops, counts, and the more powerful, if they have a case among themselves.  
78. On choosing witnesses to investigate any matter. [Col. 0552A]  
79. On the centenary’s court.
